In preparation for the 2025 elections, the KQZ introduced the PER application to facilitate the registration and voting of Albanian emigrants abroad. This initiative aims to ensure diaspora participation in the electoral process, with registration scheduled from 11 January to 11 March.<ref name="Konomi"/> To register, emigrants must provide a valid passport and a document verifying their residential address. The PER app, available for download on both mobile devices and computers, will serve as the sole method for voting from abroad. Once registered, emigrants will be removed from the domestic voter list, and by 11 May, a separate list of overseas voters will be finalised.<ref name="Konomi">{{cite web |last=Konomi |first=Esiona |work=Shqiptarja |title=Vota e diasporës në zgjedhjet 2025, regjistrimi nga 11 janari–11 mars! === Parliamentary parties ===
{{See also|List of political parties in Albania}}
As of the electoral code, a parliamentary party is defined as a political organisation that has achieved representation in the parliament by obtaining a minimum of one seat in the most recent electoral contest.{{sfn|Electoral Code|2024|p=2}} Subsequent to the [[2021 Albanian parliamentary election|2021 parliamentary election]], the PS obtained 74 of the 140 seats, emerging as the majority party.<ref name="CSIS"/><ref>{{cite web |publisher=Parliament of Albania |title=Mandatet Parlamentare 2021–2025 |url=https://kuvendiwebfiles.blob.core.windows.net/webfiles/mandatet.pdf |access-date=20 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240711072337/https://kuvendiwebfiles.blob.core.windows.net/webfiles/mandatet.pdf |archive-date=11 July 2024 |location=Tirana |language=sq |url-status=live}}</ref> The PD–AN secured 59 seats, while LSI acquired 4 seats and the PSD attained 3 seats.<ref name="CSIS"/>

== Parties and coalitions ==
According to the electoral code, each political party is mandated to submit a registration request to the [[Central Election Commission (Albania)|CEC]] no later than 70 days prior to the scheduled election date.{{sfn|Electoral Code|2024|p=34|loc=Article 64}} This request must comprehensively contain several critical components, including the identity of the party chair authorised to present candidates, the official name and acronym of the party, a specimen of the official stamp, and the contact information for both the finance officer and communication officer.{{sfn|Electoral Code|2024|p=34|loc=Article 64}} Registered political parties have the option to form coalitions, which must also be registered with the KQZ at least 60 days before the election.{{sfn|Electoral Code|2024|p=34|loc=Article 65}} A political party that is part of a coalition is restricted from engaging in another coalition or presenting candidates independently.{{sfn|Electoral Code|2024|p=34|loc=Article 65}} The coalition is required to designate a leading party, which assumes the responsibility for fulfilling the legal obligations formed in the electoral code, and to document inter-party relations in a formal coalition agreement submitted to the KQZ.{{sfn|Electoral Code|2024|p=34|loc=Article 65}} It is essential that both political parties and coalitions submit a multi-name list of candidates for the parliament election no later than 50 days prior to the election.{{sfn|Electoral Code|2024|p=35|loc=Article 67}}

In June 2024, [[Lulzim Basha]], the former leader of the [[Democratic Party of Albania|Democratic Party]], established a new faction titled, the Democratic Party–Euroatlantic Democrats, following internal conflicts regarding the ownership of the party's official seal.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=Euronews Albania |title=Basha prezanton ndryshimet në logon e Pd: Demokratët euroatlantikë |url=https://euronews.al/basha-prezanton-ndryshimet-ne-logon-e-pd-demokratet-euroatlantike/ |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241115105612/https://euronews.al/basha-prezanton-ndryshimet-ne-logon-e-pd-demokratet-euroatlantike/ |archive-date=15 November 2024 |language=sq |date=14 June 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |work=Zëri |title=Vulën e mori Berisha, Basha prezanton ndryshimet në logon e Pd-së: Demokratët Euroatlantike! |url=https://zeri.ai/politike/vulen-e-mori-berisha-basha-paralajmeron-parti-te-re-do-bej-rekurs-hyjme-i203961 |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241115104801/https://zeri.ai/politike/vulen-e-mori-berisha-basha-paralajmeron-parti-te-re-do-bej-rekurs-hyjme-i203961 |archive-date=15 November 2024 |location=Tirana |language=sq |date=14 June 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> By November 2024, Basha revealed that he was engaged in advanced discussions with [[Endri Shabani]] of {{lang|sq|[[Nisma Thurje]]|i=no}} to explore potential electoral cooperation.<ref>{{cite web |work=Dosja |title='Ka individë që kanë dhënë kontribut në kohë të vështira!' Basha: Në diskutime me Nisma Thurje për të dalë bashkë në zgjedhje |url=https://dosja.al/politike/ka-individe-qe-kane-dhene-kontribut-ne-kohe-te-veshtira-basha-ne-diskut-i401867 |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241109194559/https://dosja.al/politike/ka-individe-qe-kane-dhene-kontribut-ne-kohe-te-veshtira-basha-ne-diskut-i401867 |archive-date=9 November 2024 |location=Tirana |language=sq |date=9 November 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> However, Shabani publicly rejected the possibility of such an alliance, asserting that a cooperation with Basha or his faction was "zero".<ref>{{cite web |work=Dosja |title=Basha deklaroi se janë në diskutime për bashkëpunim në zgjedhjet e 2025, Endri Shabani e përgënjeshtron: Zero shanse! |url=https://dosja.al/politike/basha-deklaroi-se-jane-ne-diskutime-per-bashkepunim-ne-zgjedhjet-e-2025-i401868 |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241109182903/https://dosja.al/politike/basha-deklaroi-se-jane-ne-diskutime-per-bashkepunim-ne-zgjedhjet-e-2025-i401868 |archive-date=9 November 2024 |location=Tirana |language=sq |date=9 November 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 24 September 2024, representatives of the Democratic Party initiated consultations with allies for the upcoming elections, with [[Ilir Meta]] of the [[Freedom Party of Albania|Freedom Party]] being the first to meet.<ref name="PDPLSHQ">{{cite web |last=Maloku |first=Danjela |work=Shqiptarja |title=Një listë në zgjedhje? Pd nis takimet me aleatët, i pari në radhë Meta! Kreu i Pl: Duam logon tonë, por do gjejmë format më efikase |url=https://shqiptarja.com/lajm/zgjedhjet-parlamentare-noka-takohet-me-meten-diskutojne-nese-kandidatet-e-pl-do-futen-ne-lista-te-perbashketa-me-pd |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240924102516/https://shqiptarja.com/lajm/zgjedhjet-parlamentare-noka-takohet-me-meten-diskutojne-nese-kandidatet-e-pl-do-futen-ne-lista-te-perbashketa-me-pd |archive-date=24 September 2024 |language=sq |date=24 September 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> Meta did not take a clear stance on whether to run on a joint electoral list or separately, but expressed a preference for using his own party's logo.<ref name="PDPLSHQ"/> On 14 November 2024, the party's leader Sali Berisha, who was placed under house arrest since December 2023, addressed concerns about Meta's involvement in the electoral list for the elections, despite Meta's imprisonment in October 2024.<ref name="SBIMS">{{cite web |work=Syri |title=A do jetë Ilir Meta pjesë e listës?/ Berisha: I burgosur politik! Dumani, me dhunë i kërkoi Ismailit dëshmi kundër tij |url=https://www.syri.net/syri_kosova/shqiperi/564583/a-do-jete-ilir-meta-pjese-e-listes-ose-berisha-i-burgosur-politik-dumani-me-dhune-i-kerkoi-ismailit-deshmi-kunder-tij/ |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241115130335/https://www.syri.net/syri_kosova/shqiperi/564583/a-do-jete-ilir-meta-pjese-e-listes-ose-berisha-i-burgosur-politik-dumani-me-dhune-i-kerkoi-ismailit-deshmi-kunder-tij/ |archive-date=15 November 2024 |language=sq |date=14 November 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> Berisha underscored that Meta, who is according to him incarcerated without a clear charge, would be included in the electoral list if his party joined the coalition.<ref name="SBIMS"/>

By the time of the election, the [[Central Election Commission (Albania)|CEC]] had registered 53 political parties and 11 coalitions.<ref name="IFES">{{Cite web |url=https://www.ifes.org/tools-resources/election-snapshots/elections-albania |title=Election Snapshot: Elections in Albania: Parliamentary Elections May 11, 2025 |publisher=[[IFES]]}}</ref> In order to be in the ballot, parties either needed to have a certain number of MPs in the current parliament or have 5,000 signatures, while coalitions either needed to have a certain number of MPs in the current parliament or have 7,000 signatures.<ref>{{cite web |title=Republic of Albania: Parliamentary Elections: 11 May 2025 |url=https://www.osce.org/files/f/documents/2/a/584622.pdf |page=8 |publisher=OSCE}}</ref>

== Campaign ==

The campaign of this election was characterized by the vast use of social media, especially from smaller parties, as they did not have as much television access compared to larger parties.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://a2news.com/english/shqiperia/politike/fushata-zgjedhore-online-fushebeteja-e-re-politike-e-zgjedhje-i1147538|title=Online election campaign, the new political battlefield of the 2025 elections|date=9 May 2025|website=A2CNN}}</ref>

===Preceding events===
====TikTok ban====
On 21 December 2024, Prime Minister Edi Rama announced that TikTok would be banned in Albania for at least one year, starting from the beginning of 2025. Rama cited the death of a teenager in a brawl linked to a conflict on TikTok and concerns over social media promoting youth violence. Alongside this ban, the Albanian government plans to initiate educational programs for students and parents.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albania to ban TikTok for a year, blaming it for promoting violence among children | work=ABC News | date=21 December 2024 |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-12-22/albania-bans-tiktok-for-one-year/104755308?future=true&}}</ref>

On 13 March 2025, the Electronic and Postal Communications Authority (AKEP) and the National Cybersecurity Authority (AKSK), per the decisions released by the Albanian government, instructed all internet service providers in Albania to block TikTok's IPs, DNS resolution, and Server Name Indications, as well as ByteDance's IP addresses.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.panorama.com.al/qeveria-njoftoi-mbylljen-e-tiktok-zbulohet-data-ja-kur-nis-bllokimi-i-aksesit-ne-vendin-tone-per-platformen-e-rrjeteve-sociale/|title=Zbulohet data, ja kur do të mbyllet rrjeti social 'TikTok' në Shqipëri!|date=20 May 2025|website=Panorama}}</ref>

Opposition leader Sali Berisha criticized the ban, arguing it would hinder their ability to run online campaigns ahead of the elections. Hundreds of Democrat protesters gathered in front of the Kryeministria building on 15 March 2025 to protest the ban.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albanian opposition protests TikTok ban alleging censorship ahead of election |website=[[Associated Press News]] |date=15 March 2025 |url=https://apnews.com/article/albania-opposition-tiktok-ban-protest-election-db108a58f84307596e257e41567248e7}}</ref> Arlind Qori, leader of Together Movement, considered the ban as an act of censorship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://top-channel.tv/video/rama-mbyll-tiktok-shperthen-arlind-qori-akt-censure-dy-muaj-para-zgjedhjeve-breaking/|title=Rama mbyll Tiktok, SHPËRTHEN Arlind Qori: AKT CENSURE, dy muaj para ZGJEDHJEVE! | Breaking - Top Channel|website=top-channel.tv}}</ref>

The 2025 parliamentary election campaign of the Socialist Party of Albania (PS) was the fifth consecutive national campaign led by Prime Minister Edi Rama, who sought to extend his tenure beyond a decade in power. The campaign culminated in a decisive victory on 11 May 2025, with the PS securing 83 out of 140 seats in the Albanian Parliament, its strongest result to date.

Having governed since 2013, the Socialist Party entered the 2025 race with a platform centered on European Union accession, economic modernization, and institutional reform.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20250514-albania-socialist-parliamentary-elections|title=Albania PM's Socialist Party scores large victory in parliamentary elections|date=14 May 2025|website=France 24}}</ref>  The campaign was launched amid growing public fatigue with political polarization and concerns over corruption, media freedom, and democratic backsliding.

The campaign was anchored in the slogan "Albania 2030 in EU, only with Edi and SP," positioning the party as the sole credible force capable of delivering EU membership within the decade. Rama emphasized continuity, stability, and technocratic governance, highlighting achievements in infrastructure development, including road networks and urban renewal, tourism, [[Vetting law|juridical reform]] and digitalization of public services.

'''<br />'''The campaign culminated in a high-profile rally on 9 May (Europe Day) in Tirana, symbolically aligning the party's message with Albania's European aspirations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://euronews.al/en/sp-will-win-over-78-seats-rama-closes-may-11-campaign-in-tirana/|title=“SP Will Win Over 78 Seats” – Rama Closes May 11 Campaign in Tirana|first=Nen|last=Si|date=9 May 2025}}</ref>

The Socialist Party and Edi Rama ran a strong attacking campaign against the opposition and also ridiculing it, openly calling [[Sali Berisha]] "bufi" (the owl) and the Democratic Party, "këneta" (the swamp)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://a2news.com/shqiperia/politike/fare-jane-keneta-dhe-bufi-sipas-edi-rames-i1147073|title=Çfarë janë “këneta” dhe “bufi” sipas Edi Ramës?|date=3 May 2025|website=A2CNN}}</ref> Rama was also noted for using strong language to belittle and mock opponents, also specifically claiming at a rally in Dibër that "half of the men in this country are retarded".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://top-channel.tv/2025/04/17/gjysma-e-burrave-ne-kete-vend-jane-cyryke-rama-per-kryebashkiaken-e-bulqizes-kur-me-thane-qe-ishte-e-divorcuar/|title=“Gjysma e burrave në këtë vend janë çyrykë”/ Rama për kryebashkiaken e Bulqizës: Kur më thanë që ishte e divorcuar…|website=top-channel.tv}}</ref>

The Democratic Party of Albania (PD) entered the 2025 parliamentary elections under the leadership of Sali Berisha, running as part of the Alliance for a Magnificent Albania (ASHM). The campaign was launched on 11 April with a rally in Tirana's Mother Teresa Square, marking the start of a month-long effort to reclaim ground lost in previous elections.<ref>{{Cite web|title= DP starts campaign|url= https://politiko.al/english/ditari-i-opozites/nis-zyrtarisht-fushata-zgjedhore-partia-demokratike-ngre-sot-s-i529496|website= politiko.al}}</ref>

The PD's campaign centered on themes of anti-corruption, restoring democracy, and defending the vote. Berisha framed the election as a battle against what he called a "regime of theft and betrayal," accusing the ruling Socialist Party of state capture and electoral manipulation. The party adopted the slogan "Make Albania Magnificent", a deliberate echo of American populist rhetoric, and hired [[Chris LaCivita]], a U.S. political strategist known for his work on [[Donald Trump]]’s campaigns.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eliamep.gr/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Explainer_Albanian-elections-ENG.pdf|title=Albanian Elections}}</ref> The campaign emphasized juridical independence, reversation alleged politicization of institutions, economic liberalization and support for small businesses, protection of national idenitity and traditional values, return of the diaspora through tax reductions. The party also focused on increasing the minimum pension to 200 euro a month while the minimum pension at 500 euros.

Despite a high-profile campaign and aggressive rhetoric, the Democratic Party-Alliance for a Magnificent Albania secured 50 seats, down from 63 in 2021, marking one of its weakest performances in decades. The result reflected both internal fragmentation and the limited resonance of its populist messaging. Berisha’s continued leadership—despite international sanctions and legal controversies—remained a polarizing factor within the party and among voters.

===Observers===
The [[Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe]] deployed 338 officials led by [[Lamberto Zannier]] to monitor the election.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=Associated Press |title=OSCE observers launch mission to monitor Albania's upcoming parliamentary vote |url=https://apnews.com/article/albania-parliamentary-election-politics-69ca955143d989c3fe138df63f28acac |access-date=3 April 2025 |date=3 April 2025}}</ref>

=== Campaign incidents ===
==== Allegations of vote buying from PS ====
On 11 May 2025, the Democratic Party accused the Socialist Party of operating a vote-buying scheme from an office in Tirana linked to its network of patronage activists. The event was broadcast live on [[Syri Television]], showing alleged PS activists using the place to pressure voters and give benefits for political support. [[Belind Këlliçi]], the Political Leader of the Democratic Party for Tirana County, publicly called for immediate police intervention; however, the [[State Police (Albania)|police]] reportedly arrived approximately two hours later.
By the time law enforcement reached the scene, several activists and the Socialist Party MP [[Erion Braçe]] had already fled the premises, allegedly taking materials with them. Among those identified at the scene was Ledi Imeraj, Director of the National Innovation Agency.
Socialist Party MP Erion Braçe was accused not only of protecting the alleged patronage operation but also of using violence against journalist Ambrozia Meta during the live broadcast.
Although the police stated that no compromising or illegal materials were found during the search conducted in the presence of representatives from both political parties, all individuals present were escorted to Police Station No. 2 for questioning. Statements and formal complaints were filed by representatives of both parties.
The [[Special Anti-Corruption Structure]] (SPAK) opened an investigation into the case.{{efn|Attributed to multiple sources <ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.syri.net/politike/787346/syri-tv-zbulon-zyren-e-fshehte-te-patronazhisteve-ps-ne-tirane-mes-tyre-drejtoresha-e-agjencise-se-ekselences/ | title='Me lista votuesish' - Syri TV zbulon zyrën e fshehtë të patronazhistëve PS në Tiranë! ==== PD-PS Lezhë brawl ====
The opposition, led by the PD, accused members of the PS of attempting to buy votes. Andi Marku, the head of PS in Kolsh, was allegedly involved in these claims. 
Meanwhile, [[Pjerin Ndreu]], the Mayor of Lezhë, dismissed these allegations and accused PD of staging provocations. Groups of militants affiliated with both parties reportedly blocked roads, restricting movement and heightening tensions. Fatjon Zefi, the Deputy Mayor of Lezhë, was one of the individuals caught in this disruption when his vehicle was stopped, leading to a verbal and physical confrontation between PD and PS representatives. Later on, authorities stepped in to detain several individuals for questioning.<ref>{{cite web |title= Electoral incident in Lezhë. A car is stopped during the night.|url= https://top-channel.tv/2025/05/06/incident-zgjedhor-ne-lezhe-ndalohet-nje-makine-gjate-nates-ndreu-militante-me-arme-levizin/ |access-date= 6 May 2025}}</ref>

==== Allegations of vote buying from PSD ====
Allegations of vote-buying involving the Social Democratic Party (PSD) surfaced in Malësi e Madhe, particularly in Koplik. Ardian Hysa, the head of PSD in Malësi e Madhe, was investigated for allegedly attempting to buy votes. Authorities also scrutinized Florenc Kalaj, a local resident suspected of facilitating the process. Police uncovered WhatsApp messages suggesting coordination between PSD representatives and voters regarding financial incentives. SPAK authorized searches of Hysa's business and personal property as part of the probe.<ref>{{cite web |title= Chairman of PSD in Malësi e Madhe accused of vote buying|url= https://newsbomb.al/politike/kryetari-i-psd-ne-malesine-e-madhe-nen-hetim-per-e-zgjedhore-zbarhd-i362582 |access-date= 6 May 2025}}</ref>


== Conduct and irregularities ==

=== International observation ===
ODIHR's final report characterized the election as competitive and professionally conducted, and noted that the election administration generally managed the process inclusively and transparently. At the same time, it found that contestants did not enjoy a level playing field. According to ODIHR, the ruling Socialist Party benefited from administrative resources during the campaign, which created an undue incumbency advantage; the report also cited pressure on voters, especially public employees, and stated that existing electoral legislation and its narrow interpretation by the election administration did not prevent abusive practices.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" /> The international observation mission's preliminary statement reached a similar conclusion immediately after election day, saying that candidates could mostly campaign freely but that the election was marked by widespread misuse of public resources and institutional power by the ruling party, as well as reports of pressure and intimidation.<ref name="OSCEPAStatement2025">{{cite web |date=12 May 2025 |title=Albania's parliamentary elections competitive and well run but lacked level playing field, international observers say |url=https://www.oscepa.org/en/news-a-media/press-releases/2025/albanias-parliamentary-elections-competitive-and-well-run-but-lacked-level-playing-field-international-observers-say |publisher=[[OSCE Parliamentary Assembly]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>

The same report stressed that voting on election day was generally calm and transparent, but that observers noted procedural shortcomings, pressure on voters, cases of intimidation, interference by party observers or affiliates, inducements, allegations of vote buying and a frequent compromise of ballot secrecy because of polling-station layout, overcrowding or interference.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" /> ODIHR also reported that the count was orderly in many places but affected by delays, a chaotic atmosphere in some locations, last-minute changes to counting-team members and disputes over out-of-country ballots from Greece.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

=== Use of state resources and incumbency advantage ===
A central criticism of the election concerned the Socialist Party's use of state resources and public office. ODIHR found that the ruling party benefited from widespread use of administrative resources and institutional leverage, which blurred the line between state and party and undermined equal opportunities for contestants.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" /> The final report also noted that public institutions' social-media activity created campaign-related violations, while the CEC's monitoring and enforcement remained limited in scope and effectiveness.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

The issue was reinforced by the structure of public power at the time of the vote. The Socialist Party controlled the national government, held an overwhelming majority of municipalities after the [[2023 Albanian local elections]], and had governed continuously since 2013. Opposition parties argued that this enabled the party to combine public administration, municipal employment, welfare benefits, permits and informal patronage networks with the campaign. ODIHR did not verify every opposition claim, but it stated that allegations of pressure on public employees and misuse of patronage networks were inconsistent with international standards.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

The 2025 election also followed the partial electoral reform of July 2024, which retained a mixed candidate-list model with a closed-list component. ODIHR reported that several smaller parties argued the system favoured the two largest parties and enabled party leaders to retain significant control over parliamentary representation, partly because of weak internal party democracy.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" /> Smaller and newer parties also argued that the requirement to submit full candidate lists in every district imposed disproportionate organizational burdens, limiting the competitiveness of the contest.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

=== Pressure, patronage networks and vote buying allegations ===
Vote buying, patronage and intimidation were among the most frequently raised concerns. ODIHR noted reports of vote buying, attempts to unduly influence vulnerable voters, intimidation of opposition supporters, pressure on public employees, and alleged criminal influence on the election in some areas.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" /> The report also stated that a new coordination mechanism between SPAK, the CEC and the General Prosecutor's Office may have had a deterrent effect, but that some interlocutors questioned the effectiveness of efforts against politically connected organized crime.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

On election day, the Democratic Party accused the Socialist Party of operating an office in Tirana connected to patronage activists and alleged that lists of voters were being used to monitor or influence turnout. Local reporting showed Democratic Party representatives and journalists confronting persons at the site, while police later said no illegal materials had been found and that people from both sides had been escorted for questioning. The case was referred to SPAK. Because most immediate reports on the incident came from party-aligned media, the article treats the episode as an allegation rather than an established finding; however, the broader themes of voter pressure and patronage networks were also recorded by ODIHR.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

=== Campaign finance and public spending ===
The ODIHR final report stated that shortcomings in campaign-finance rules affected transparency and equality of opportunity. It noted that key ODIHR recommendations on campaign finance had not been addressed, including the absence of interim reporting, the lack of specific rules on loans, online campaigning and third-party expenditures, and ambiguities about whether candidate spending counted toward party limits.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" /> Although contestants were legally required to publish databases of donations or loans, ODIHR reported that none did so, and that the CEC lacked effective legal instruments to enforce compliance.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

The spending environment became politically sensitive because the election was held shortly after major public-procurement and municipal corruption investigations. Opposition parties alleged that public tenders, infrastructure spending and municipal jobs functioned as indirect campaign tools for the incumbent party. These allegations were not all adjudicated during the campaign, but post-election corruption proceedings against Deputy Prime Minister Belinda Balluku and earlier proceedings involving Tirana mayor Erion Veliaj reinforced the political significance of public-procurement issues during and after the campaign.<ref name="OCCRPVeliaj2025" /><ref name="ReutersBallukuProbe2026" />

=== Media coverage and information environment ===
The media environment was another major issue. ODIHR concluded that the independence, diversity and integrity of news content were undermined by non-transparent financing, concentrated ownership, interference in editorial autonomy and political influence. It also reported that the majority of media outlets were perceived to be aligned with the ruling party, and that the Socialist Party and the Democratic Party dominated monitored television news coverage, while unattributed campaign coverage was common and no effective measures were taken against it.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

A separate BIRN Albania monitoring report, based on data from the Audiovisual Media Authority, found that the 2025 campaign coverage on the 18 main central television stations was dominated by the two largest political forces and that smaller parties were marginalized. BIRN wrote that the monitoring revealed persistent imbalances, limited pluralism and the dominance of major political actors.<ref name="BIRNMediaArticle2025">{{cite web |date=4 December 2025 |title=New BIRN Albania Report Reveals Imbalances in Audiovisual Media Coverage during 2025 Elections |url=https://birn.eu.com/news-and-events/report-reveals-imbalances-in-audiovisual-media-coverage/ |website=[[Balkan Investigative Reporting Network]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> In news bulletins on the three main private national broadcasters, [[Top Channel]], [[TV Klan]] and [[Vizion Plus]], BIRN found that the Socialist Party received 52% of electoral-subject airtime, compared with 44.5% for the Alliance for a Magnificent Albania and less than 4% for all other electoral subjects combined.<ref name="BIRNMedia2025">{{cite web |date=December 2025 |title=Albania's Parliamentary Elections 2025: Audiovisual Media Monitoring |url=https://birn.eu.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Audiovisual-Media-Monitoring-ENG.pdf |website=[[Balkan Investigative Reporting Network]] |format=PDF |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> On the same three private national broadcasters, BIRN found that Edi Rama dominated individual-actor news coverage with 49.4% of airtime, compared with 42% for Sali Berisha and 7.8% for all other actors.<ref name="BIRNMedia2025" />

The strongest imbalance on some stations was visible in live campaign coverage. BIRN reported that ABC News allocated 73.4% of live campaign-broadcast airtime to the Socialist Party and 26.1% to the Alliance for a Magnificent Albania, with 0.5% for other electoral subjects.<ref name="BIRNMedia2025" /> Klan News allocated 54.7% of news-bulletin airtime to the Socialist Party and 44.6% to the Alliance, leaving 0.6% for all other electoral subjects; ABC News allocated 51.4% to the Socialist Party, 47.4% to the Alliance and 1.2% to others.<ref name="BIRNMedia2025" /> BIRN also noted that paid political-advertising patterns differed by outlet and that, on Top News, the Socialist Party aired 132.5 minutes of advertisements compared with 4.5 minutes by the Alliance for a Magnificent Albania.<ref name="BIRNMedia2025" />

=== Digital campaigning and TikTok ban ===
Digital campaigning was especially important in 2025, particularly for smaller parties that lacked access to major television platforms. The government banned [[TikTok]] shortly before the election, arguing that it was necessary to address youth violence and social harm. Opposition parties and some civil-society figures described the ban as censorship and said that it disproportionately harmed challengers who relied on online campaigning. ODIHR did not assess the ban as an electoral crime, but it stated that the government's TikTok ban limited some candidates' campaign opportunities and that no authority had been designated to monitor manipulative online campaign content.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

ODIHR also noted that campaigning on social networks was not regulated, that several contestants disseminated divisive or manipulative content, and that third-party accounts reportedly used coordinated inauthentic behaviour to amplify attacks against the opposition.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" /> These findings were significant because the campaign combined a high-volume online environment with weak oversight, strong polarization and unequal access to traditional broadcast media.

=== Out-of-country voting and ballots from Greece ===
The 2025 election was the first Albanian parliamentary election in which citizens abroad were able to vote by post. IFES reported that 3,713,761 voters were registered, including 245,935 voters abroad, while the IPU later recorded 3,713,897 registered voters and 1,664,873 voters overall.<ref name="IFES2025">{{cite web |date=11 May 2025 |title=Elections in Albania: Parliamentary Elections May 11, 2025 |url=https://www.ifes.org/tools-resources/election-snapshots/elections-albania |publisher=[[International Foundation for Electoral Systems]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="IPU2025">{{cite web |title=Albania Parliament May 2025 Election |url=https://data.ipu.org/parliament/AL/AL-LC01/election/AL-LC01-E20250511/ |publisher=[[Inter-Parliamentary Union]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> ODIHR described the introduction of out-of-country voting as an important milestone and found that the process was generally well managed, while also noting that it was highly challenging because of late legal adoption, ballot-delivery problems and disputes during the count.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

A dispute developed over ballots mailed from Greece. Democratic Party officials alleged irregularities, including claims that some citizens in Greece had not received ballots while large numbers of completed ballots arrived for counting. The CEC briefly suspended or reviewed aspects of the process following opposition complaints, but later resumed counting after CEC chair [[Ilirjan Celibashi]] stated that the Democratic Party had not provided proof sufficient to invalidate the ballots. The dispute contributed to the opposition's refusal to recognize the result, but the official result was certified by the election administration and later reflected in international parliamentary databases.<ref name="IPU2025" />

== Aftermath ==

=== Domestic reactions ===
[[Sali Berisha]], [[Democratic Party of Albania|opposition]] leader and chairman of the [[Alliance for a Magnificent Albania]], refused to recognize the outcome of the election, and called for a protest on 16 May.<ref>{{Cite news |date=13 May 2025 |title=Berisha refuses to concede defeat, calls for protests, as Socialists secure fourth term in landslide 2025 victory |url=https://albaniantimes.al/berisha-refuses-to-concede-defeat-calls-for-protests-as-socialists-secure-fourth-term-in-landslide-2025-victory/ |access-date=14 May 2025 |work=Albanian Times}}</ref>

=== 2025–2026 opposition protests ===
{{Main|2025–2026 Albanian opposition protests}}

Following the election, the opposition continued to reject the result, with [[Sali Berisha]] and the [[Democratic Party of Albania|Democratic Party]] alleging that the vote had been stolen and demanding new elections.<ref name="Reuters-Election-2025">{{cite news |date=13 May 2025 |title=Albania's Rama wins historic fourth term, opposition says vote stolen |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/albanias-rama-on-brink-landslide-election-win-2025-05-13/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> International observers described the election as competitive and professionally managed, but also reported that contestants did not enjoy a level playing field and cited misuse of public resources, pressure on public employees, intimidation and vote-buying concerns.<ref name="OSCE-ODIHR-2025">{{cite web |date=23 October 2025 |title=Albania's parliamentary elections competitive and professionally managed, but lacked a level playing field |url=https://odihr.osce.org/odihr/elections/albania/600169 |website=[[OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights]] |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>

The post-election dispute later became part of a broader protest wave against Prime Minister [[Edi Rama]] and his government. From November 2025 to May 2026, the Democratic Party and allied opposition groups organized demonstrations in [[Tirana]], demanding Rama's resignation, a technocratic government and new elections. The protests intensified after corruption proceedings involving Deputy Prime Minister [[Belinda Balluku]], which the opposition used to support wider accusations of corruption and state capture.<ref name="Reuters-Parliament-2025">{{cite news |date=18 December 2025 |title=Albanian parliament erupts over corruption allegations against deputy PM |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/albanian-parliament-erupts-over-corruption-allegations-against-deputy-pm-2025-12-18/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="Reuters-Dec22-2025">{{cite news |date=22 December 2025 |title=Corruption charges spark protests against Albanian government |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/corruption-charges-spark-protests-against-albanian-government-2025-12-22/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>



The post-election protest cycle widened after SPAK's corruption case against Deputy Prime Minister Belinda Balluku. Reuters reported that Balluku was accused of interfering in two construction tenders from 2021 worth more than €200 million and that the case threatened to weaken Albania's EU accession drive because it involved one of Rama's closest allies.<ref name="ReutersBallukuProbe2026" /> In December 2025, protesters hurled petrol bombs at the government building after prosecutors indicted Balluku and requested parliamentary authorization for her arrest; Balluku denied the accusations and said she would cooperate with the judiciary.<ref name="ReutersProtestsBalluku2025">{{cite news |date=22 December 2025 |title=Corruption charges spark protests against Albanian government |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/corruption-charges-spark-protests-against-albanian-government-2025-12-22/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> Rama dismissed Balluku in February 2026 after months of public pressure, while Reuters reported that EU officials were closely watching the government's handling of corruption cases.<ref name="ReutersBallukuFired2026" />

Several demonstrations involved clashes between protesters and police. Protesters used Molotov cocktails, fireworks and flares, while police responded in some cases with tear gas and water cannon. In February 2026, violent anti-government protests in Tirana resulted in injuries and arrests, while demonstrators continued to demand Rama's resignation and government accountability over corruption allegations.<ref name="AP-Feb10-2026">{{cite news |date=10 February 2026 |title=Violence breaks out at anti-government protest in Albanian capital |url=https://apnews.com/article/albania-antigovernment-protest-clashes-corruption-31cf7519545985569f1e9de1f9a7c506 |work=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="AlJazeera-Feb21-2026">{{cite news |date=21 February 2026 |title=Clashes in Albania as protesters demand PM Rama resign |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/21/clashes-in-albania-as-protesters-demand-pm-rama-resign |work=[[Al Jazeera English]] |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Certification and legal challenges ===
After the vote, the CEC completed the certification process and the newly elected legislature first convened on 12 September 2025. The [[Inter-Parliamentary Union]] recorded that the Socialist Party retained its majority with 83 seats, while the Democratic Party-led Alliance for a Magnificent Albania won 50 seats, the Social Democratic Party won 3, the Opportunity Party won 2, and NISMA–SHB and Lëvizja Bashkë won 1 each.<ref name="IPU2025" /> [[Niko Peleshi]] of the Socialist Party was elected Speaker of the new legislature at its first session.<ref name="IPU2025" />

The Democratic Party rejected the result and filed complaints over alleged irregularities, including claims linked to the out-of-country vote from Greece. The CEC maintained that the opposition had not provided sufficient evidence to invalidate the disputed ballots, while international observers stated that the election was competitive and professionally managed but did not provide contestants with a level playing field.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" /> The gap between certification by election institutions and rejection by the main opposition became a central element of the post-election crisis and later opposition protests.

A candidate can win the presidency in a single round by either winning over 45% of the vote or if they win 40% of the vote while finishing more than 10 [[percentage points]] ahead of the second-place candidate. If no candidate meets either threshold, a runoff takes place between the top two candidates.{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/oct/23/argentina-elections-2015-a-guide-to-the-parties-polls-and-electoral-system |title=Argentina elections 2015: a guide to the parties, polls and Milei in his victory speech vowed to begin "the reconstruction of Argentina" and end the country's economic decline.{{Cite news |last1=Misculin |first1=Nicolás |last2=Elliott |first2=Lucinda prospective foreign minister Diana Mondino also announced Argentina would pause their accession to [[BRICS]].{{Cite news |date=20 November 2023 |title=China reaffirms support for new nations joining BRICS as Argentina signals rejection |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/china-reaffirms-support-new-nations-joining-brics-argentina-signals-rejection-2023-11-20/ conceded and announced his retirement from politics after the runoff election results showed that he had lost by roughly 11 percentage points.{{Cite web |last=Sugarman |first=Jacob |date=20 November president [[Alberto Fernández]] congratulated Milei: "I am a man of democracy, and I value nothing more than the popular verdict. I trust that tomorrow we can start working with Javier Milei to guarantee an orderly transition."{{Cite news |date=20 November 2023 |title=Global leaders react to Milei's Argentina victory |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/latin-american-leaders-react-argentina-election-result-2023-11-20/ |access-date=20 November 2023 |archive-date=20 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120074604/https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/latin-american-leaders-react-argentina-election-result-2023-11-20/ |url-status=live}} Former president [[Mauricio Macri]], who had endorsed Milei in the runoff, said: "I congratulate Javier Milei for bravely representing the will to advance and prosper that lives in the hearts of Argentines. He knew how to listen to the voice of young people and the fatigue of millions of neglected and impoverished people." ===International=== {{Flag|Bolivia}}: Bolivian president [[Luis Arce]] wished success to Javier Milei and said that he would work hard to keep "firm relations" with Argentina. On the other hand, former president [[Evo Morales]] said that he would never wish success to "[Milei's] fascism, far-right and neoliberalism, who supports the Zionist genocide and [[American imperialism|Yankee imperialism]]."{{cite news |title=Presidente de Bolivia desea "éxitos" a Milei y dice que trabajará por relaciones "firmes" |url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/spa/argentina-transici%C3%B3n_presidente-de-bolivia-desea--%C3%A9xitos--a-milei-y-dice-que-trabajar%C3%A1-por-relaciones--firmes-/48993046 |access-date=25 November 2023 |agency=SwissInfo |date=20 November 2023 |language=es |archive-date=25 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125110708/https://www.swissinfo.ch/spa/argentina-transici%C3%B3n_presidente-de-bolivia-desea--%C3%A9xitos--a-milei-y-dice-que-trabajar%C3%A1-por-relaciones--firmes-/48993046 |url-status=live}}{{cite news |title=Evo Morales, sobre la victoria de Milei: "Nunca le vamos a desear éxito al al fascismo, ultraderechismo y neoliberalismo" |url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/politica/evo-morales-sobre-la-victoria-de-milei-nunca-le-vamos-a-desear-exito-al-al-fascismo-ultraderechismo-nid21112023/ |access-date=25 November 2023 |work=La Nación |date=21 November 2023 |language=es |archive-date=25 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125110709/https://www.lanacion.com.ar/politica/evo-morales-sobre-la-victoria-de-milei-nunca-le-vamos-a-desear-exito-al-al-fascismo-ultraderechismo-nid21112023/ |url-status=live}} {{Flag|Brazil}}: Brazilian president [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] congratulated Milei without mentioning his name, saying: "Democracy is the voice of the people, and it must always be respected. My congratulations to Argentine institutions for conducting the electoral process and to the Argentine people who participated on election day in an orderly and peaceful manner. I wish the new government good luck and success." Former president [[Jair Bolsonaro]] congratulated Milei saying: "Congratulations to the Argentine people for Javier Milei's victory. Hope will shine again in South America. May these good winds reach the United States and Brazil so that honesty, progress and freedom come back to all of us." {{Flag|Chile}}: Chilean president [[Gabriel Boric]] congratulated Milei saying: "I salute Javier Milei for his victory and Sergio Massa for his worthy recognition of defeat. I wish the Argentine people the best and know that they will always have our respect and support. As president of Chile, I will work tirelessly to keep our sister nations united and collaborating for the well-being of all." {{Flag|China}}: Chinese president [[Xi Jinping]] congratulated Milei saying: "I am ready to work with President-elect Milei to continue the China-Argentina friendship, help the development and revitalisation of our respective countries through win-win cooperation, and promote steady and far-reaching development of China-Argentina relations." Milei thanked Xi for his congratulations, replying "I thank President Xi Jinping for the congratulations and good wishes. I send him my most sincere wishes for the Chinese people's wellbeing."{{Cite news |date=2023-11-23 |title=Argentina's Milei thanks Chinese president, in softening of tone |language=en |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/argentinas-milei-thanks-chinese-president-softening-tone-2023-11-23/ |access-date=2023-11-23 |archive-date=23 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123123816/https://www.reuters.com/world/argentinas-milei-thanks-chinese-president-softening-tone-2023-11-23/ |url-status=live}} {{Flag|Colombia}}: Colombian president [[Gustavo Petro]] lamented Milei's win, which was mocked by El Salvador president [[Nayib Bukele]]. {{Flag|European Union}}: [[Charles Michel]], the [[president of the European Council]], congratulated Milei saying: "Congratulations to Argentina's new president-elect Javier Milei for his victory. The people of Argentina have spoken in free and democratic elections."{{cite web |title=European Union, Indian PM congratulate Javier Milei on Argentina election win |url=https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/argentina/european-union-congratulates-javier-milei-on-argentina-election-win.phtml |publisher=[[Buenos Aires Times]] |access-date=23 November 2023 |date=20 November 2023 |archive-date=23 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123072857/https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/argentina/european-union-congratulates-javier-milei-on-argentina-election-win.phtml |url-status=live}} [[Ilan Goldfajn]], the president of the [[Inter-American Development Bank]], congratulated Milei saying: "Congratulations Javier Milei, president-elect of Argentina. At the IDB, we are ready to continue our collaboration with the country and promote sustainable and inclusive economic development for the benefit of its citizens." {{Flag|India}}: Indian prime minister [[Narendra Modi]] congratulated Milei saying: "Congratulations for the victory in the Presidential elections. These members serve in the [[45th Canadian Parliament]]. Governor General [[Mary Simon]] dropped the [[writs of election]] on March 23, 2025,{{cite news |url=https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p2/2025/2025-03-24-x3/html/si-tr58-eng.html |title=Canada Gazette, Part 2, Volume 159, Number 3: Proclamation Issuing Election Writs |date=March 24, 2025}} after Prime Minister [[Mark Carney]] advised her to [[Dissolution of Parliament in Canada|dissolve Parliament]]. This was the first election to use a new [[2022 Canadian federal electoral redistribution|343-seat electoral map]] based on the [[2021 Canadian census|2021 census]]. Key issues of the election campaign included the [[cost of living]], housing, crime, [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|U.S. tariffs against Canadian exports]], and [[American expansionism under Donald Trump|threats of annexation]] made by U.S. president [[Donald Trump]].{{cite news |last=Stevis-Gridneff |first=Matina |date=April 28, 2025 |title=What's at Stake in Canada's Elections? The Key Issues for Voters |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/28/world/canada/canada-election-issues-voters.html |access-date=April 29, 2025 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331}} The [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]] won a fourth term, emerging with a [[minority government]] for a third consecutive election.{{cite web |last=Cecco |first=Leyland |date=April 29, 2025 |title=Canada's liberal party, led by Mark Carney, secures election victory after dramatic reversal of fortune |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/apr/29/canada-election-result-liberal-win-mark-carney-anti-trump |access-date=May 1, 2025 |website=The Guardian}}{{cite web |last=Schmunk |first=Rhianna |date=April 29, 2025 |title=Canada election: Liberals will form next government, CBC News projects |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/livestory/canada-election-liberals-will-form-next-government-cbc-news-projects-9.6738893 |access-date=May 1, 2025 |website=CBC News }}{{cite web |date=April 29, 2025 |title=Carney's Liberals beat Conservatives, CTV News declares, will form minority government |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/canadians-give-liberals-4th-mandate-as-carney-leads-party-to-minority-win/ |access-date=April 29, 2025 |website=CTV News}} The election marked the first time they won the popular vote [[2015 Canadian federal election|since 2015]], doing so with the highest vote share for any party in a federal election [[1984 Canadian federal election|since 1984]], and their own highest vote share [[1980 Canadian federal election|since 1980]]. The party's victory came after a substantial rebound in the polls, noted as being "one of the widest on record in any democracy". The election also saw the highest turnout [[1993 Canadian federal election|since 1993]], with 69.5% of Canada's 28{{nbsp}}million eligible voters casting a ballot. Both the Liberal Party and the [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative Party]] improved upon their vote share and seat count [[2021 Canadian federal election|from 2021]], while the other parties all lost ground; this was the most concentrated the popular vote had been in support of the top two parties [[1958 Canadian federal election|since 1958]], with over 85% voting Liberal or Conservative.{{Cite web |title=Résultats Canada - 3795 Election Politique Citoyen |url=https://www.election-politique.com/resultats.php?num=3795&k=CA&kr=&pol=p2 |access-date=May 28, 2025 |website=www.election-politique.com}} Consequently, the election delivered the [[New Democratic Party]] (NDP) their worst result in its history, as it received just over six percent of the popular vote and only won seven seats. As a result, the NDP lost [[official party status]] for the first time since 1993.{{cite web |last1=Trinh |first1=Judy |title=Orange crushed: What's next for the NDP |date=April 30, 2025 |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/federal-election-2025/article/orange-crushed-whats-next-for-the-ndp/ |work=CTV |access-date=April 30, 2025}} The concentration of support for the two major parties was identified by commentators as marking a polarization in Canadian politics and a shift towards a [[two-party system]]. The result was a reversal of polling trends lasting from mid-2023 to January 2025, which had led to projections of the Conservatives winning in a landslide.{{Cite news |last=Coletta |first=Amanda |date=April 29, 2025 |title=In stunning comeback, Carney's Liberals win Canada's federal election |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2025/04/28/canada-election-results-carney-win-liberals-trump/ |access-date=April 30, 2025 |newspaper=The Washington Post|issn=0190-8286}} Carney's [[2024–2025 Canadian political crisis|replacement]] of [[Justin Trudeau]] as [[Leader of the Liberal Party of Canada|leader of the Liberal Party]] played a key role in the turnaround. With his extensive experience as a central banker and his perceived competence, Carney was seen as better equipped to handle the [[2025 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico|trade war launched by the U.S.]] and other major economic issues.{{cite web |title=A stunning reversal of fortunes in Canada's historic election |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c78jv246n91o |website=BBC News |date=April 27, 2025 |access-date=May 1, 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Micek |first1=John L. |title='Trump wanted to break us,' Canadian leader says after stunning turnaround victory |url=https://www.masslive.com/politics/2025/04/trump-wanted-to-break-us-canadian-leader-says-after-romping-to-victory.html |website=Masslive|date=April 29, 2025 |access-date=May 1, 2025}} Two sitting party leaders failed to win re-election to their parliamentary seats: [[Pierre Poilievre]] of the Conservative Party and [[Jagmeet Singh]] of the NDP.{{Cite web |title=Get live results from the Canadian federal election |url=https://newsinteractives.cbc.ca/elections/federal/2025/results/ |access-date=April 29, 2025 |website=CBC News}}{{cite news |last1=Hauen |first1=Jack |last2=Cross |first2=Jessica |title=Jagmeet Singh loses seat, resigns on disastrous night for NDP |url=https://www.elliotlaketoday.com/2025-federal-election-news/jagmeet-singh-loses-seat-resigns-on-disastrous-night-for-ndp-10585278 |access-date=April 29, 2025 |agency=Elliot Lake Today |date=April 29, 2025}} Poilievre had held his riding of Carleton since 2004, and his defeat was regarded as a significant setback for the Conservatives; he was the first Conservative leader to lose their seat since [[Kim Campbell]] in 1993. ==Background== The [[2021 Canadian federal election]], held on September 20, 2021, saw only minor changes from the preceding [[2019 Canadian federal election|2019 election]].{{cite news |date=September 24, 2021 |orig-date=September 21, 2021 |title=Justin Trudeau to Remain Prime Minister of Canada |url=https://www.nytimes.com/live/2021/09/20/world/canada-election-2021 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111083150/https://www.nytimes.com/live/2021/09/20/world/canada-election-2021 |archive-date=January 11, 2022 |access-date=September 21, 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]]}} The incumbent [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]], led by Prime Minister [[Justin Trudeau]], did not win the popular vote and failed to win enough seats to gain a parliamentary majority, winning only a plurality of seats and retaining its status as a minority government. The [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative Party]] won the popular vote and continued as the [[Official Opposition (Canada)|Official Opposition]].{{Cite news |date=September 21, 2021 Following [[2022 Conservative Party of Canada leadership election|a leadership election]], [[Pierre Poilievre]] was elected the new leader of the Conservative Party. Because of the decennial redrawing of riding boundaries, many MPs were running in districts that had changed.{{cite web |date=March 23, 2025 |title=Redistribution of Federal Electoral Districts 2022 |url=https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=res&dir=cir/red&document=index&lang=e |access-date=May 1, 2025 |website=Elections Canada}}{{cite news |date=March 23, 2025 |title=Redrawn ridings could give Conservatives an advantage, say pollsters |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/redrawn-ridings-could-give-conservatives-an-advantage-say-pollsters/ |access-date=May 1, 2025 |agency=The Canadian Press |via=CTV News}} === Government transition === {{main|2024–2025 Canadian political crisis|2025 Liberal Party of Canada leadership election}} Despite low government approval ratings and a large polling lead for the opposition Conservatives{{snd}}linked to an ongoing cost of living crisis{{snd}}Trudeau had insisted he would lead the Liberals into the next general election, and attempt to win a fourth consecutive term. Despite his commitment to seek re-election, pressure on Trudeau to step aside had been mounting from the Liberal caucus after [[by-election]] losses in [[Safe seat|safe]] Liberal seats.{{Cite news plunged into a [[political crisis]] when finance minister [[Chrystia Freeland]] abruptly resigned, only hours before she was set to present the government's fall economic statement.{{Cite web |last=Tasker |first=John Paul |date=December 16, 2024 |title=Chrystia Freeland resigns from Trudeau's cabinet and sources say Dominic LeBlanc will replace her deputy PM resigns from cabinet as tensions with Trudeau rise over Trump tariffs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/dec/16/chrystia-freeland-resigns-canada-trump |access-date=April 24, 2025 |work=The Guardian|issn=0261-3077}} Trudeau, who had already faced down a caucus revolt in October, was faced with renewed questions about his leadership.{{Cite news |last=Tasker |first=John Paul |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-faces-frustrated-mps-after-chrystia-freeland-s-shock-resignation-1.7411380 |access-date=March 28, 2025 |work=[[CBC News]]}} By December 22, 21 Liberal MPs had publicly called for Trudeau to step down.{{Cite news |last=Maharaj |first=Mayson |date=December 22, 2024 |title=Most Liberals in caucus want Trudeau to go, says longtime loyalist |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/liberal-mp-majority-trudeau-resign-1.7417503 |access-date=March 28, 2025 |work=[[CBC News]]}} On January 6, 2025, Trudeau announced his intention to resign as prime minister after the party elected his successor.{{cite news |date=January 6, 2025 |title=Justin Trudeau promises to resign as prime minister and Liberal leader after leadership race |url=https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/justin-trudeau-promises-to-resign-as-prime-minister-and-liberal-leader-after-leadership-race/article_5c5ba5ec-cc34-11ef-88f1-577060db4a8c.html |access-date=January 6, 2025 |work=Toronto Star}} The ensuing leadership election was won by [[Mark Carney]], former [[governor of the Bank of Canada]] and [[governor of the Bank of England]].{{Cite web |last1=Aiello |first1=Rachel |last2=Nersessian |first2=Mary |last3=Hahn |first3=Phil |date=March 9, 2025 |title=Results are in, Mark Carney wins Liberal leadership race. Follow for live updates. |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/new-threats-demand-new-ideas-mark-carney-addresses-liberals-after-landslide-win-recap-full-event/ |access-date=March 9, 2025 |website=CTVNews}} Carney was sworn in as prime minister on March 14, becoming the first prime minister to have never held elected public office prior to their appointment.{{cite web |last=Tunney |first=Catharine |date=March 9, 2025 |title=In landslide win, Liberal Party chooses Mark Carney as new leader and next PM |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/liberal-pary-leadership-winner-1.7476359 |url-status=live |archive-date=March 14, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250314202958/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/liberal-pary-leadership-winner-1.7476359 |access-date=April 29, 2025 |website=[[CBC News]]}}{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mark-carney-be-sworn-canadian-prime-minister-now-must-face-trump-2025-03-14/ |title=Mark Carney sworn in as Canada's prime minister, says he can work with Trump |last1=Mukherjee |first1=Promit |last2=Ljunggren |first2=David |date=March 14, 2025 |work=Reuters |access-date=April 29, 2025}} The crisis occurred against the backdrop of [[Donald Trump]]'s victory in the [[2024 United States presidential election]] and his threats to impose sweeping tariffs on Canada. Disagreements over how to handle this threat were seen as being a contributor to the Trudeau ministry's collapse.{{Cite web |date=December 17, 2024 |title=Trudeau in peril after spat over Trump threat sparks crisis |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5y49ym6em3o |access-date=April 24, 2025 |website=BBC}}{{Cite web |date=January 7, 2025 |title=Trump's trolling and tariffs sped up Trudeau's demise. Guardian|issn=0261-3077}} === Date of the election === {{See also|Electoral Participation Act#Movement of fixed election date}} Under the [[Fixed election dates in Canada|fixed-date provisions]] of the ''[[Canada Elections Act]]'', which requires federal elections to be held on the third Monday in October in the fourth calendar year after the polling day of the previous election, the election was scheduled to take place on October 20, 2025.{{cite web |date=May 3, 2007 |title=An Act to amend the Canada Elections Act |url=https://www.parl.ca/documentviewer/en/39-1/bill/C-16/third-reading/page-27?col=2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240626012317/https://www.parl.ca/documentviewer/en/39-1/bill/C-16/third-reading/page-27?col=2 |archive-date=June 26, 2024 |archive-format=PDF |access-date=June 25, 2024 |publisher=LegisINFO }} However, elections can occur before the scheduled date if the [[Governor general of Canada|governor general]] dissolves Parliament on the recommendation of the prime minister, either for a [[List of snap elections in Canada|snap election]] or after the government loses a vote on a [[Loss of supply|supply bill]] or a specific [[motion of no confidence]].{{Cite web |title=Majority and Minority Governments |url=https://learn.parl.ca/understanding-comprendre/en/how-parliament-works/majority-and-minority-governments/ |access-date=March 30, 2025 |website=Parliament of Canada}} On March 20, 2024, the government introduced the ''[[Electoral Participation Act]]'', which included an amendment to the ''Canada Elections Act'' that would have changed the fixed election date to October 27, 2025, to avoid conflicting with [[Diwali]], as well as [[2025 Alberta municipal elections|municipal elections in Alberta]].{{cite Hansard |jurisdiction=Canada |title=Canada Elections Act |url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/Content/House/441/Debates/292/HAN292-E.PDF |house=[[House of Commons of Canada]] |date=March 20, 2024 |page=21765}}{{cite web |url=https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/minister-leblanc-introduces-legislation-to-further-strengthen-canada-s-electoral-process-863933578.html |title=Minister LeBlanc introduces legislation to further strengthen Canada's electoral process |publisher=CNW | access-date=March 22, 2024 |date=March 20, 2024}} The bill died on the [[Order Paper|order paper]] when the Parliament of Canada was [[Prorogation in Canada|prorogued]] by Prime Minister Justin Trudeau after he announced his resignation.{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Dale |date=January 14, 2025 |title=Death on the order paper |url=https://nationalmagazine.ca/en-ca/articles/law/hot-topics-in-law/2025/death-on-the-order-paper |access-date=March 30, 2025 |work=National Magazine}} On March 23, 2025, after a request from Prime Minister Mark Carney, the Governor General dissolved parliament and called an election for April 28, 2025.{{Cite web |title=Canada election live: Canadian PM Mark Carney calls snap election |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cwyd2x7xxwet |access-date=March 23, 2025 |website=BBC News}} The date fixed for the return of the writs by the Chief Electoral Officer was May 19, 2025. Voters select a representative nominated for their [[Electoral district (Canada)|electoral district]] (sometimes referred to as a ''riding''), and the candidate with more votes than any other candidate is elected to a seat in the 343-member House of Commons and represents that riding as its [[member of parliament]] (MP). The party that wins the most seats in the House of Commons usually forms government, with that party's leader becoming [[Prime Minister of Canada|prime minister]]. The largest party by seat count that is not the government or part of a governing coalition becomes the Official Opposition. That party receives more finances and privileges than the other opposition parties.{{cite web |title=The Official Opposition in the Canadian House of Commons |first=Jay |last=Makarenko |date=January 30, 2008 |website=re:politics |url=https://repolitics.com/features/the-official-opposition-in-the-canadian-house-of-commons/ |access-date=March 27, 2025}}{{cite web |title=Selection and Role of Canada's Official Opposition |first=Susan |last=Munroe |date=February 27, 2019 |website=ThoughtCo |url=https://www.thoughtco.com/official-opposition-508467 |access-date=March 27, 2025}} An absolute [[majority]] of the votes cast is not needed to form government and is rarely achieved by any single party. Additionally, the government party does not need to obtain a majority of the seats in the House of Commons; under the current multi-party system, it is common for the government party to lack a majority. However, to pass bills, the governing party must have support of a majority of MPs. Without majority support, the government [[motion of no confidence|can be defeated]], then a new party is named government or an election has to be held. ====Redistribution==== {{main|2022 Canadian federal electoral redistribution}} [[File:Canada Election 2021 Results Map (New Boundaries).svg|thumb|250x250px|The transposed results of the 2021 election, if they had taken place under the 2023 Representation Order

Invitations were issued on the basis of meeting at least two of three conditions: having at least one sitting MP, recording at least 4% support in national opinion polling, and endorsing candidates in at least 90 percent of ridings.{{cite web |title=Leaders' Debates Commission invites leaders to the next leaders' debates |url=https://www.debates-debats.ca/en/news/2025/commission-invites-leaders-debates/index.htm |website=[[Leaders' Debates Commission]] |access-date=April 1, 2025 |date=April 1, 2025}} The Green Party's invitation was rescinded on April 16 as it ultimately ran candidates in 232 ridings (less than 70 percent) despite earlier submitting to the Commission that it would run candidates in every riding.{{Cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/green-party-debate-commission-rules-candidate-numbers-1.7509867 |title=Debates commission defends inviting Greens despite party's candidate shortage |first=Darren |last=Major |work=CBC News |date=April 14, 2025 |access-date=April 14, 2025}}{{Cite web |date=April 16, 2025 |title=Green Party dropped from leaders' debates for not running criteria of either holding a seat in Parliament or polling at least 4%.{{cite web |date=March 24, 2025 |title=Leaders' Debates Commission announces dates, location for upcoming debates, and leader participation decision date |url=https://www.debates-debats.ca/en/news/2025/debate-dates-announced/index.htm |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=[[Leaders' Debate The Commission declined to reschedule the debate to a different day, but agreed to move the start time two hours earlier to 6:00 pm [[Eastern Daylight Time|EDT]].{{cite news |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/11132946/canada-election-leaders-debate-french-postponement-montreal-canadiens-game/ |title=French election debate time moved to avoid Montreal Canadiens game conflict |first=Sean |last=Previl |work=[[Global News]] |date=April 15, 2025 |access-date=April 16, 2025}} A post-debate news scrum after the French language debate was dominated by the far-right ''[[Rebel News]]'' and other right-wing media outlets, leading to complaints from other journalists at the event.{{cite web |title='Canadians deserve better,' Voters are disappointed after Leaders' Debates Commission cancelled post-debate scrums due to security concerns |first=Beatriz |last=Ferreira |date=April 18, 2025 |website=[[NOW Toronto]] |url=https://nowtoronto.com/news/voters-are-disappointed-after-leaders-debates-commission-cancelled-post-debate-scrums-due-to-security-concerns/ |access-date=April 19, 2025}} Michel Cormier, the commission's executive director, responded that he was "unaware" that ''Rebel News'' and another organization associated with ''Rebel'' founder [[Ezra Levant]] were registered as third-party advertisers with Elections Canada.{{cite news |title=Debates commission unaware Rebel News registered as advocacy group, official says |first=Darren |last=Major |work=CBC News |date=April 17, 2025 |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/rebel-news-rightwing-media-press-conferences-debates-1.7512714 |access-date=April 19, 2025}}{{cite news |title=Party leaders didn't take media questions after the English debate.
