== Aftermath ==
[[Tanel Kiik]], the vice-chair of the Centre Party, had said that "the Centre Party would be satisfied if it were to get 20 seats" in the Riigikogu, while [[Sven Mikser]], the former chairman of the SDE, said that "nine mandates is probably the best the party can do in Estonia today".<ref name=":12">{{Cite news |date=5 March 2023 |title=Live blog: 2023 Riigikogu elections |url=https://news.err.ee/1608905171/live-blog-2023-riigikogu-elections |access-date=5 March 2023 |newspaper=Err |archive-date=5 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230305174320/https://news.err.ee/1608905171/live-blog-2023-riigikogu-elections |url-status=live}}</ref> Ratas later described the results as "mediocre".<ref name=":12" /> After the publication of e-vote results, Kallas gave a speech and thanked her voters.<ref name=":12" /><ref name=":16" /> Kallas was congratulated by [[Sanna Marin]], the prime minister of Finland, and [[Krišjānis Kariņš]], the prime minister of Latvia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marin |first=Sanna |date=6 March 2023 |title=Warm congratulations to PM @kajakallas on your success in the Estonian parliamentary elections. Looking forward to continuing our close cooperation in EU affairs, NATO and security policy and our support to Ukraine. |url=https://twitter.com/MarinSanna/status/1632642358603833346 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306123605/https://twitter.com/MarinSanna/status/1632642358603833346 |archive-date=6 March 2023 |access-date=6 March 2023 |website=Twitter}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 March 2023 |title=Kariņš congratulates Kallas on Estonian election success |url=https://eng.lsm.lv/article/politics/politics/karins-congratulates-kallas-on-estonian-election-success.a499432/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306123605/https://eng.lsm.lv/article/politics/politics/karins-congratulates-kallas-on-estonian-election-success.a499432/ |archive-date=6 March 2023 |access-date=6 March 2023 |website=LSM}}</ref>

[[Martin Helme]], the leader of EKRE, stated that "he does not trust the e-vote results" and demanded a recount.<ref name=":12" /><ref name=":16">{{Cite web |date=5 March 2023 |title=Riigikogu Parliamentary elections were held in [[Croatia]] on 17 April 2024 to elect the members of the 11th [[Sabor]]. Prior to the elections, the government consisted of a coalition of the [[Croatian Democratic Union]] and [[Independent Democratic Serb Party]], with parliamentary support of five [[national minority]] MPs, two MPs from the [[Croatian Social Liberal Party]] and [[Croatian Demochristian Party]], and one independent MP, [[Silvano Hrelja]].

The ruling centre-right HDZ won the most seats for the fourth straight election, defeating the centre-left [[Rivers of Justice]] alliance. The right-wing populist [[Homeland Movement (Croatia)|Homeland Movement]] finished third, with the left-wing and green [[We Can! (Croatia)|We Can!]] in fourth place. The HDZ subsequently formed a right-wing coalition with the Homeland Movement and returned HDZ leader [[Andrej Plenković]] as Prime Minister for a third term.<ref>{{cite news |title=Croatia's Ruling Party Reaches Coalition Deal With Right Wing|url=https://www.barrons.com/news/croatia-conservatives-reach-coalition-deal-with-right-wing-spokesman-f0697844 |work=Barron's |date=May 8, 2024|author=Lajla Veselica}}</ref>

==Background==
The pre-election period was marked by speculation about the possible date of the election, potential coalitions and unification of the opposition, as well as accusations of corruption and nepotism in the government led by Prime Minister [[Andrej Plenković]] and his changes in ministers.

=== Changes of ministers in the government ===
Plenković's two governments were marked by many changes in ministerial positions, a total of 30 ministers. Of its initial lineup in 2016, only [[Nina Obuljen Koržinek]] ([[Ministry of Culture and Media (Croatia)|Minister of Culture and Media]]), the Deputy Prime Minister [[Oleg Butković]] ([[Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure|Minister of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure]]), and the Deputy Prime Minister [[Tomo Medved]] ([[Ministry of Croatian Veterans|Minister of Croatian Veterans]]) remained.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Deželić |first=Vanja |date=12 December 2023 |title=Ovo su svi ministri koji su otišli ili ih je Andrej Plenković smijenio |trans-title=These are all the ministers who left or were dismissed by Andrej Plenković |url=https://n1info.hr/vijesti/ovo-su-svi-ministri-koji-su-otisli-ili-ih-je-andrej-plenkovic-smijenio/ |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=N1 |language=hr |archive-date=18 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240218192556/https://n1info.hr/vijesti/ovo-su-svi-ministri-koji-su-otisli-ili-ih-je-andrej-plenkovic-smijenio/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[The Bridge (Croatia)|The Bridge]] ministers [[Vlaho Orepić]] ([[Ministry of the Interior (Croatia)|Minister of the Interior]]), [[Ante Šprlje]] ([[Ministry of Justice and Public Administration (Croatia)|Minister of Justice]]), and [[Slaven Dobrović]] ([[Ministry of Environmental Protection and Energy (Croatia)|Minister of Environmental Protection and Energy]]) were the first to leave the [[Cabinet of Andrej Plenković I|government]]. They were dismissed by Plenković for refusing to reject the vote of no confidence in [[Zdravko Marić]] ([[Ministry of Finance (Croatia)|Finance Minister]]) requested by the opposition. Immediately afterwards, fourth The Bridge member [[Ivan Kovačić]] ([[Ministry of Public Administration (Croatia)|Minister of Administration]]) resigned from the government, as did [[Pavo Barišić]] ([[Ministry of Science and Education (Croatia)|Minister of Education]]) who was facing accusations of plagiarism which were later dismissed by the [[University of Augsburg]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Srzić |first=Ante |date=13 December 2023 |title=Od neposlušnih mostovaca do zbunjenog Filipovića: Tko je sve odletio iz Plenkovićeve vlade |trans-title=From disobedient Most ministers to confused Filipović: Who flew away from Plenković's government |url=https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/od-neposlusnih-mostovaca-do-zbunjenog-filipovica-tko-je-sve-odletio-iz-plenkoviceve-vlade-foto-20231213 |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=tportal.hr |archive-date=18 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240218191054/https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/od-neposlusnih-mostovaca-do-zbunjenog-filipovica-tko-je-sve-odletio-iz-plenkoviceve-vlade-foto-20231213 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Scandals occurred in 2018, which began with the Borg affair that led to the departure of Economy Minister [[Martina Dalić]] and her replacement by [[Darko Horvat (politician)|Darko Horvat]], who was incarcerated in [[Remetinec prison]] in 2022 after being charged with illegally awarding 2.6 million Kuna.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> [[Davor Ivo Stier]] ([[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Croatia)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]]) resigned after a disagreement with the party leadership, and his successor [[Marija Pejčinović Burić]] left in 2019 after being elected [[Secretary General of the Council of Europe]]. In 2019, five ministers left the government following a series of scandals. [[Lovro Kušćević]] (Minister of Construction and Spatial Planning) after it was found that he conducted illegal real estate brokerage while he was the mayor of [[Nerežišća]] on [[Brač]], [[Goran Marić (politician)|Goran Marić]] (Minister of State Property) resigned after a series of real estate scandals. An indictment against [[Gabrijela Žalac]] ([[Ministry of Regional Development and EU Funds (Croatia)|Minister of Regional Development and European Union Funds]]) was brought for abuse of position and authority in the "Software affair", and her name was also mentioned in the Vjetroelektrana affair with [[Josipa Rimac]]. [[Tomislav Tolušić]] ([[Ministry of Agriculture (Croatia)|Minister of Agriculture]]) was mentioned in numerous scandals and was later indicted for embezzlement with EU funds, including 2.5 million Kuna for his winery, which he received under irregular circumstances.<ref name=":1" /> [[Nada Murganić]] ([[Ministry of Labour and Pension System, Family and Social Policy|Minister of Demography, Family, Youth and Social Policy]]) was dismissed for unsatisfactory performance.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ivandić |first=Ivana |date=31 December 2019 |title=Smjena Nade Murganić i povećanje porodiljnih naknada obilježili su socijalnu politiku |trans-title=The dismissal of Nada Murganić and the increase in maternity benefits marked social policy |url=https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/smjena-nade-murganic-i-povecanje-porodiljnih-naknada-obiljezili-su-socijalnu-politiku-20191231 |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=tportal.hr |language=hr |archive-date=18 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240218191056/https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/smjena-nade-murganic-i-povecanje-porodiljnih-naknada-obiljezili-su-socijalnu-politiku-20191231 |url-status=live }}</ref>

More controversies occurred in 2020, with [[Milan Kujundžić]] ([[Ministry of Health (Croatia)|Minister of Health]]) leaving the government following a series of real estate scandal. [[Damir Krstičević]] ([[Ministry of Defence (Croatia)|Minister of Defence]]) resigned after the crash of a military training plane in which two members of the [[Croatian Air Force]] died near Biljana Donje near [[Zadar]]. He was replaced by [[Mario Banožić]], who left after committing manslaughter while driving irresponsibly.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> [[Marko Pavić]] was removed as Ministry of Regional Development and EU Funds, along with [[Gari Cappelli]] ([[Ministry of Tourism and Sports (Croatia)|Minister of Tourism]]).<ref name=":0" /> [[Vesna Bedeković]] was replaced as Minister for Demography, Family, Youth and Social Policy by [[Josip Aladrović]], who himself was under investigation by [[USKOK]] and also resigned.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> [[Nataša Tramišak]] was replaced as Minister of Regional Development and European Union Funds by [[Šime Erlić]] as part of Plenković's personal intentions. [[Ivan Paladina]], Minister of Spatial Planning, Construction and State Property, was removed due to the slow pace of reconstruction after [[2020 Zagreb earthquake|Zagreb]] and [[2020 Petrinja earthquake|Petrinja earthquakes]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

=== Election date ===
In 2023, it was reported that the HDZ was preparing to hold elections in April 2024, two months before the [[2024 European Parliament election|elections for members of the European Parliament]]. From conversations with several high-ranking HDZ members, ''[[Jutarnji list]]'' reported that that Andrej Plenković would collect advantages with which he will go before the voters and ask for another prime ministerial mandate in the next year, so that the elections can be held before the [[Easter]] holidays in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 January 2023 |title=HDZ se priprema za parlamentarne izbore u ožujku 2024. |trans-title=HDZ is preparing for parliamentary elections in March 2024. |url=https://dubrovacki.slobodnadalmacija.hr/dubrovnik/vijesti/hrvatska-i-svijet/hdz-se-priprema-za-parlamentarne-izbore-u-ozujku-2024-1259610 |access-date=26 January 2023 |website=Dubrovački vjesnik |language=hr |archive-date=26 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230126091826/https://dubrovacki.slobodnadalmacija.hr/dubrovnik/vijesti/hrvatska-i-svijet/hdz-se-priprema-za-parlamentarne-izbore-u-ozujku-2024-1259610 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Information subsequently began to circulate that the Parliament could be dissolved on 22 March, the last day of the 21st session of the Croatian Parliament, and the dissolution could be voted on.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Penić |first1=Goran |last2=Špoljar |first2=Marko |date=28 February 2024 |title=HDZ datumom skupa u Lisinskom otkrio kada ćemo na birališta!? Bit će neradna |date=15 March 2024 |url=https://www.glasistre.hr/hrvatska/2024/03/15/milanovic-objavio-datum-izbora-prvi-put-ikada-glasat-cemo-u-srijedu-bit-ce-neradna-921250 |publisher=Glas Istre |access-date=15 March 2024 |archive-date=15 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240315112455/http://www.glasistre.hr/hrvatska/2024/03/15/milanovic-objavio-datum-izbora-prvi-put-ikada-glasat-cemo-u-srijedu-bit-ce-neradna-921250 |url-status=live }}</ref> while the [[2000 Croatian parliamentary election]] was held on a Monday.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ovo nije prvi put da na parlamentarne izbore izlazimo na radni dan: Evo kada se zadnji put to dogodilo |date=15 March 2024 |url=https://www.jutarnji.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/ovo-nije-prvi-put-da-na-parlamentarne-izbore-izlazimo-na-radni-dan-evo-kada-se-zadnji-put-to-dogodilo-15439362 |publisher=Jutarnji List |access-date=15 March 2024 |archive-date=15 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240315130646/https://www.jutarnji.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/ovo-nije-prvi-put-da-na-parlamentarne-izbore-izlazimo-na-radni-dan-evo-kada-se-zadnji-put-to-dogodilo-15439362 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 28 July 2023, a coalition was agreed between two liberal regional parties, the [[Istrian Democratic Assembly]] and the [[Alliance of Primorje-Gorski Kotar]], with a main goal to represent [[Istria]] and [[Kvarner Gulf|Kvarner]] in [[Electoral district VII (Croatian Parliament)|VII]] and [[Electoral district VIII (Croatian Parliament)|VIII]] electoral districts. The coalition will also contest the 2024 European Parliament elections.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 July 2023 |title=IDS i PGS zajedno na europarlamentarne i parlamentarne izbore |trans-title=IDS and PGS together in the European parliamentary and parliamentary elections |url=https://vijesti.hrt.hr/hrvatska/ids-a-i-pgs-a-zajedno-na-europarlamentarnim-i-parlamentarnim-izbora-10927238 |access-date=20 December 2023 |website=HRT |language=hr |archive-date=25 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125115757/https://vijesti.hrt.hr/hrvatska/ids-a-i-pgs-a-zajedno-na-europarlamentarnim-i-parlamentarnim-izbora-10927238 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1 August 2023 |title=Paus: IDS potpisivanjem koalicije s PGS-om ulazi u borbu za 4. mandat na parlamentarnim izborima i gradi širu koaliciju za europske izbore |trans-title=Paus: IDS, by signing a coalition with PGS, enters the fight for the 4th mandate in the parliamentary elections and builds a wider coalition for the European elections |url=https://5portal.hr/vijesti_detalj.php?id=43808 |access-date=20 December 2023 |website=5portal |language=hr |archive-date=20 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231220210912/https://5portal.hr/vijesti_detalj.php?id=43808 |url-status=live }}</ref> Two more liberal parties, [[Focus (Croatian political party)|Focus]] and the [[People's Party – Reformists]] announced their cooperation on 10 November 2023. The leader of the Reformists [[Radimir Čačić]] said that with a high level of certainty they expect a large expansion of this cooperation with parties close to them, who believe that Croatia is institutionally and as a society trapped by the HDZ, and that this should be stopped and space should be opened for a different, much more modern, more liberal Croatia.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 November 2023 |title=Fokus i Reformisti potpisali predizbornu koaliciju: "S HDZ-om ni pod koju cijenu" |trans-title=Fokus and the Reformists signed a pre-election coalition: "Not with HDZ at any cost" |url=https://www.novilist.hr/novosti/hrvatska/fokus-i-reformisti-potpisali-predizbornu-koaliciju-s-hdz-om-ni-pod-koju-cijenu/?meta_refresh=true |access-date=20 December 2023 |website=Novi List |language=hr |archive-date=20 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231220210911/https://www.novilist.hr/novosti/hrvatska/fokus-i-reformisti-potpisali-predizbornu-koaliciju-s-hdz-om-ni-pod-koju-cijenu/?meta_refresh=true |url-status=live }}</ref> Finally two groups made one single alliance on 9 December 2023. The most anticipated coalition of the 2024 election was an alliance of the main opposition party [[Social Democratic Party of Croatia]] and left wing contender [[We Can! (Croatia)|We Can!]] (Možemo!). Such an idea was seen as probable because of similar policies of the parties. We Can! announced on 27 June 2023 that it would run separately, leaving the possibility after the election to form a government with parties of the center to the left, including the SDP.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 June 2023 |title=Možemo! na izbore izlazi samostalno: 'Istraživanje je pokazalo da stranke tako dobivaju više glasova' |trans-title=We Can! goes to the elections independently: 'Research has shown that parties get more votes this way' |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/mozemo-ili-ne-mozemo-tomaseviceva-stranka-objavljuje-hoce-li-u-koaliciju-s-sdp-om-1690696 |access-date=30 December 2023 |website=Večernji list |language=hr |archive-date=30 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231230204620/https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/mozemo-ili-ne-mozemo-tomaseviceva-stranka-objavljuje-hoce-li-u-koaliciju-s-sdp-om-1690696 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 1 March 2024, [[Sandra Benčić]] (We Can!) announced the start of negotiations with the SDP on a "dotted coalition", which means a coalition in constituencies where they do not have enough support individually. In that case, the coalition would be implemented in IV., V., VII. and IX. electoral unit, while in other units the parties would go separately.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kolar |first=Helena |date=1 March 2024 |title=Benčić potvrdila: 'Kreću pregovori sa SDP-om o točkastoj koaliciji' |trans-title=Benčić confirmed: 'Negotiations with the SDP on a point coalition are underway' |url=https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/bencic-potvrdila-krecu-pregovori-sa-sdp-om-o-tockastoj-koaliciji/ |access-date=2 March 2024 |language=hr |archive-date=2 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240302100137/https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/bencic-potvrdila-krecu-pregovori-sa-sdp-om-o-tockastoj-koaliciji/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 22 March 2024 Možemo and SDP announced that an agreement was not reached, which means that they will go separately in all constituencies.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 March 2024 |title=Propali su pregovori između SDP-a i Možemo, Benčić poručila: "Nema razdora, cilj nam i dalje ostaje isti – srušiti HDZ" |trans-title=The negotiations between the SDP and Možemo failed, Benčić said: "There is no discord, our goal remains the same – to overthrow the HDZ." |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/propali-su-pregovori-izmedju-sdp-a-i-mozemo---839413.html?itm_source=BottomNews&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |access-date=22 March 2024 |website=Dnevnik.hr |language=hr |archive-date=22 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240322234759/https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/propali-su-pregovori-izmedju-sdp-a-i-mozemo---839413.html?itm_source=BottomNews&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 17 February 2024, members of the left-liberal opposition held a [[2024 Zagreb protest|protest]] under the name "Enough! Let's Go to the Elections!" ({{langx|hr|Dosta je! Odmah na izbore!}}). The protest was organized by SDP, We Can!, [[Centre (Croatian political party)|Centre]], IDS, HSS and [[Workers' Front (Croatia)|RF]], Focus, SD, NS-Reformists, [[Civic Liberal Alliance|GLAS]], and [[Party with a First and Last Name|SsIP]]. The reason for the protest was the appointment of Judge Ivan Turudić as the [[State's Attorney Office of the Republic of Croatia|Attorney General]]. The day before, the same parties submitted a request for the dissolution of parliament and the holding of early elections. Most and HS joined them with signatures even if they did not participate in the protests.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 February 2024 |title=Oporba najavila prosvjed: "Građani žele smjenu vlasti. ==Electoral system==
{{Main|Elections in Croatia#Parliamentary Elections|}}
[[File:Constituencies of Croatia (2023-present).svg|thumb|300x300px|Electoral districts in use from 2023]]
The 151 members of the [[Croatian Parliament]] are elected from 10 geographical and two special electoral districts:<ref>[http://www.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2077_B.htm Electoral system] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113112025/http://www.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2077_B.htm |date=13 January 2016 }} IPU</ref>
*140 seats are elected in ten geographical 14-seat electoral districts ([[Croatian Parliament electoral districts|1st–10th Electoral Districts]]) by [[open list]] [[proportional representation]] (using a 5% [[electoral threshold]]) with seats allocated using the [[d'Hondt method]]
**A voter can give their "preference vote" to a single candidate on the list, but only candidates who have received at least 10% of the party's votes take precedence over the other candidates on the list.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.zakon.hr/z/355/Zakon-o-izborima-zastupnika-u-Hrvatski-sabor | title=Zakon o izborima zastupnika u Hrvatski sabor (Act on Election of Representatives to the Croatian Parliament) | language=hr | access-date=27 August 2018 | archive-date=28 August 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828035834/https://www.zakon.hr/z/355/Zakon-o-izborima-zastupnika-u-Hrvatski-sabor | url-status=live }}</ref>
*3 seats are elected in a special electoral district ([[Electoral district XI (Croatian Parliament)|11th Electoral District]]) for Croatian citizens [[Croatian diaspora|living abroad]]
*8 seats are elected from an electoral district for national minorities ([[Electoral district XII (Croatian Parliament)|12th Electoral District]]): 3 seats for Serbian, 1 seat for Italian, 1 seat for Hungarian, 1 seat for Czech and Slovak, 1 seat for Albanian, Bosniak, Macedonian, Montenegrin and Slovenian, and 1 seat for Austrian, Bulgarian, German, Jewish, Polish, Roma, Romanian, Rusyn, Russian, Turkish, Ukrainian and Vlach national minority
**Voters with the right to vote in the 12th Electoral District can choose to either vote for a candidate list on the ballot in the district they belong to according to their place of residence (one of the 10 geographical districts) or for a candidate of their minority in the 12th Electoral District.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zakon o izborima zastupnika u Hrvatski sabor (pročišćeni tekst) |url=https://www.zakon.hr/z/355/Zakon-o-izborima-zastupnika-u-Hrvatski-sabor |website=zakon.hr |access-date=2 April 2024 |archive-date=28 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828035834/https://www.zakon.hr/z/355/Zakon-o-izborima-zastupnika-u-Hrvatski-sabor |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 28 October 2022, the [[Constitutional Court of Croatia|Constitutional Court]] issued a warning that it could declare the next elections unconstitutional unless the electoral law was changed, due to excessive differences in the number of voters for each constituency, leading to significant variations in vote weight.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 October 2022 |title=Novo upozorenje Ustavnog suda: 'Ne bude li promjena izbornih jedinica, sljedeći izbori mogli bi biti proglašeni neustavnima' |trans-title=New warning from the Constitutional Court: 'If electoral units are not changed, the next elections could be declared unconstitutional' |url=https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/s-ustavnog-suda-stigao-alarm-vrijeme-je-za-promjenu-granica-izbornih-jedinica-20221027 |access-date=7 January 2023 |website=tportal.hr |language=hr |archive-date=7 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230107205007/https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/s-ustavnog-suda-stigao-alarm-vrijeme-je-za-promjenu-granica-izbornih-jedinica-20221027 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 7 February 2023, the Constitutional Court repealed the electoral law because the difference in vote weight between different electoral districts was too large to comply with the constitutional provision that each vote must be of equal weight.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 February 2023 |title=Ustavni sud ukinuo Zakon o izbornim jedinicama: "Ovo nije nikakva hajka" |trans-title=The Constitutional Court repealed the Law on Electoral Units: "This is not a scam" |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/predsjednik-ustavnog-suda-miroslav-separovic-o-zakonu-o-izbornim-jedinicama---765008.html |website=dnevnik.hr |language=Croatian |access-date=18 February 2023 }}</ref> Parliament passed a new electoral law on 20 October 2023, which came into effect on 3 November, requiring the next elections to be held with reorganized electoral districts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zakon o izbornim jedinicama za izbor zastupnika u Hrvatski sabor |url=https://www.zakon.hr/z/3574/Zakon-o-izbornim-jedinicama-za-izbor-zastupnika-u-Hrvatski-sabor |access-date=23 November 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Submission of candidate lists ===
Lists for the election of representatives may be proposed independently by one political party or by two or more political parties (coalition list) which are registered in the Republic of Croatia on the day the Decision to call the elections is announced, or by voters. Voters shall propose independent candidate lists on the basis of validly collected 500 signatures of residents of the Electoral District the list is running in.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elections of representatives to the Croatian Parliament |url=https://www.izbori.hr/site/en/about-elections-referenda/elections-of-representatives-to-the-croatian-parliament/1724 |website=izbori.hr |publisher=State Electoral Commission of the Republic of Croatia |access-date=2 April 2024 |archive-date=2 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240402234732/https://www.izbori.hr/site/en/about-elections-referenda/elections-of-representatives-to-the-croatian-parliament/1724 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Electoral lists ==
On 30 March 2024, the State Electoral Commission of the Republic of Croatia (DIP) made decisions on validly submitted lists in I. – XI. electoral district and validly proposed candidates in XII. electoral district. All decisions on validly submitted lists and validly proposed candidates and summary lists were published on the same day at 5:00 p.m. on the website of the DIP.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 March 2024 |title=10. priopćenje o objavi pravovaljano predloženih lista i kandidata i zbirnih lista na izborima zastupnika u Hrvatski sabor |trans-title=10. announcement on the publication of validly proposed lists of candidates and summary lists for the elections of deputies to the Croatian Parliament |url=https://www.izbori.hr/site/UserDocsImages/2024/Izbori_za_zastupnike_u_Hrvatski_sabor/Priop%C4%87enja/10.%20Priop%C4%87enje%20-%20objava%20pravovaljanih%20lista%20i%20kandidata%20i%20zbirnih%20lista.pdf |access-date=30 March 2024 |website=Državno izborno povjerenstvo |language=hr |archive-date=30 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240330230037/https://www.izbori.hr/site/UserDocsImages/2024/Izbori_za_zastupnike_u_Hrvatski_sabor/Priop%C4%87enja/10.%20Priop%C4%87enje%20-%20objava%20pravovaljanih%20lista%20i%20kandidata%20i%20zbirnih%20lista.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> The table below is a list of the main parties and electoral coalitions which are contesting the election.

===Female representation===
It is required by the election law that each list running in the election contains at least 40% of both men and women, to ensure equality. For the lists that do not adhere to this rule, the State Electoral Commission (DIP) will report them to The Ombudsperson for Gender Equality and the [[State's Attorney Office of the Republic of Croatia]] (DORH) when the parties and candidates proposing those lists can expect a fine of up to 33 000 [[euros]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Zakon o izborima zastupnika u Hrvatski sabor |trans-title=The Elections of representatives to the Croatian Parliament Act |url=https://www.zakon.hr/z/355/Zakon-o-izborima-zastupnika-u-Hrvatski-sabor |access-date=13 April 2024 |work=[[Narodne Novine]] |publisher=zakon.hr |date=1 January 2020 |language=Croatian |archive-date=28 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828035834/https://www.zakon.hr/z/355/Zakon-o-izborima-zastupnika-u-Hrvatski-sabor |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Strankama koje neće imati dovoljno žena na listama prijeti i do 33.000 eura kazne |url=https://n1info.hr/vijesti/strankama-koje-nece-imati-dovoljno-zena-na-listama-prijeti-i-do-33-000-eura-kazne/ |website=n1info.hr |date=27 March 2024 |access-date=13 April 2024 |archive-date=9 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409024622/https://n1info.hr/vijesti/strankama-koje-nece-imati-dovoljno-zena-na-listama-prijeti-i-do-33-000-eura-kazne/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Thirty-two out of 165 lists did not respect the rule and will be reported. A number of the main parties respected the rule and have at least six women and men on all their lists, among them Focus/Republic (11 lists), MOST/HS (11), RF (10), the Rivers of Justice coalition (10) and the Our Croatia coalition (eight). On the other hand, the biggest offenders are HDZ, DP/PiP coalition and MP Karolina Vidović Krišto's party OiP. For both HDZ and OiP, the fine could be high as much as 60 000 euros all together. When asked about this, [[Andrej Plenković]] responded: "There are many more women than 30, but the circumstances are such that we have a lot of candidates, we try to balance it ... ."<ref>{{cite web |title=Predali liste pa prekršili Zakon: Vidović Krišto rekorderka, HDZ-u kazna od 60.000 eura |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/cijena-neravnoteze-vidovic-kristo-i-hdz-u-prijeti-najveca-kazna-zbog-nedovoljno-zena-na-listama-1759343 |website=vecernji.hr |publisher=Večernji list |access-date=13 April 2024 |archive-date=16 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240416055004/https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/cijena-neravnoteze-vidovic-kristo-i-hdz-u-prijeti-najveca-kazna-zbog-nedovoljno-zena-na-listama-1759343 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Plenković o manjku žena na listama HDZ-a: Takve su okolnosti, nastojimo balansirati |url=https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/plenkovic-o-manjku-zena-na-listama-hdza-takve-su-okolnosti-nastojimo-balansirati/2551825.aspx |website=index.hr |publisher=Index |access-date=13 April 2024 |archive-date=16 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240416030959/https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/plenkovic-o-manjku-zena-na-listama-hdza-takve-su-okolnosti-nastojimo-balansirati/2551825.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>

While We Can! holds the record for the most women holding the first place on their lists (six constituencies), HDZ and DP/PiP have none.<ref>{{cite web |title=Plenković se razmeće izjavama o ravnopravnosti, a na listama nema nijedne nositeljice. Gdje su HDZ-u žene? |url=https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/plenkovic-se-razmece-izjavama-o-ravnopravnosti-a-na-listama-nema-nijedne-nositeljice-gdje-su-hdz-u-zene/ |website=telegram.hr |publisher=Telegram |access-date=13 April 2024 |archive-date=8 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240308133705/https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/plenkovic-se-razmece-izjavama-o-ravnopravnosti-a-na-listama-nema-nijedne-nositeljice-gdje-su-hdz-u-zene/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Domovinski pokret predao liste: Penava otkrio tko su nositelji, komentirao i Milanovića |url=https://direktno.hr/direkt/domovinski-pokret-objavio-nositelje-lista-penava-otkrio-dobro-poznata-imena-341825/ |website=direktno.hr |access-date=13 April 2024 }}{{Dead link|date=April 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Campaign==
The official [[political campaign]] started on 30 March with the DIP publishing all of the valid lists. It will last until the end of 15 April as the [[election silence]] is enforced. It starts at midnight and lasts until 7:00 pm on the election day when the polling stations close and [[exit polls]] are published.<ref>{{cite web |title=DIP objavio pravovaljane liste. Službeno je počela kampanja |url=https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/dip-objavio-pravovaljane-liste-sluzbeno-je-pocela-kampanja/2552266.aspx |website=index.hr |publisher=Index |access-date=13 April 2024 |date=30 March 2024 |archive-date=2 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240402211845/https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/dip-objavio-pravovaljane-liste-sluzbeno-je-pocela-kampanja/2552266.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Broje se zadnji dani kampanje: Hoćete li izaći na izbore? |url=https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/broje-se-zadnji-dani-kampanje-hocete-li-izaci-na-izbore-20240412 |website=tportal.hr |publisher=Tportal |access-date=13 April 2024 |date=12 April 2024 |archive-date=13 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413000448/https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/broje-se-zadnji-dani-kampanje-hocete-li-izaci-na-izbore-20240412 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The campaign was marked by increased [[social media advertising]] and [[content creation]]. Many politicians have, in order to appeal to young voters, joined social media platforms like [[TikTok]], among the most prominent ones being Prime Minister [[Andrej Plenković]] and the Diaspora candidate [[Ljubo Ćesić Rojs]]. The platforms are still being used mostly for critique, negativity and [[personal attacks]] on opponents. ===Issues===
On 12 January 2024, President [[Zoran Milanović]] publicly [[outing|outed]] HDZ minister [[Damir Habijan]] as gay.<ref>{{cite web |title=Milanović: Habijan je gej |trans-title=Milanović: Habijan is gay |url=https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/milanovic-habijan-je-gej/2528567.aspx |website=index.hr |publisher=Index |access-date=13 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=12 January 2024 |archive-date=15 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240215154022/https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/milanovic-habijan-je-gej/2528567.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref> It was the first case of outing a political opponent as part of [[LGBT community]] without their approval in the political history of the country. The situation caused a wave of reactions, but [[LGBT rights organizations]] did not react and a rift was created between the activists of the community.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zagreb Pride o Milanovićevom 'outanju' Habijana: 'Nismo željeli javno reći svoj stav zbog dva razloga' |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/zagreb-pride-o-milanovicevom-outanju-habijana-nismo-zeljeli-javno-reci-svoj-stav-zbog-dva-razloga-1740673 |website=vecernji.hr |publisher=Večernji list |access-date=13 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=22 January 2024 |archive-date=28 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240328140059/https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/zagreb-pride-o-milanovicevom-outanju-habijana-nismo-zeljeli-javno-reci-svoj-stav-zbog-dva-razloga-1740673 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Velika podjela u hrvatskoj gay zajednici: Aktivisti su se nakon Milanovićevog 'outanja' Habijana ozbiljno razišli |url=https://www.jutarnji.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/velika-podjela-u-hrvatskoj-gay-zajednici-aktivisti-su-se-nakon-milanovicevog-outanja-habijana-ozbiljno-razisli-15417893 |website=jutarnji.hr |publisher=Jutarnji list |access-date=13 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=21 January 2024 |archive-date=22 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240322083547/https://www.jutarnji.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/velika-podjela-u-hrvatskoj-gay-zajednici-aktivisti-su-se-nakon-milanovicevog-outanja-habijana-ozbiljno-razisli-15417893 |url-status=live }}</ref> In April, [[Zagreb Pride]] released a [[controversial]] list of candidates running who are members of the community. The list of 11 candidates, mostly members of [[We Can! (Croatia)|We Can!]], included three incumbent [[HDZ]] officials who either hadn't publicly announced their orientation before or didn't give permission to be on the list, as well as two [[Social Democratic Party of Croatia|SDP]] candidates. Politicians like [[Peđa Grbin]] (SDP) and [[Damir Vanđelić]] (Republic) condemned the list.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zagreb Pride: Ovo je 11 gej kandidata na listama. Trojica su iz HDZ-a |url=https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/zagreb-pride-ovo-je-11-gej-kandidata-na-listama-trojica-su-iz-hdza/2556118.aspx |website=index.hr |publisher=Index |access-date=13 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=13 April 2024 |archive-date=13 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413185044/https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/zagreb-pride-ovo-je-11-gej-kandidata-na-listama-trojica-su-iz-hdza/2556118.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Političari složni: Zagreb Pride nije imao pravo "outati" one koji to nisu učinili sami |url=https://n1info.hr/vijesti/politicari-slozni-zagreb-pride-nije-imao-pravo-outati-one-koji-to-nisu-ucinili-sami/ |website=n1info.hr |publisher=N1 |access-date=13 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=13 April 2024 |archive-date=13 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413173747/https://n1info.hr/vijesti/politicari-slozni-zagreb-pride-nije-imao-pravo-outati-one-koji-to-nisu-ucinili-sami/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the campaign, Zoran Milanović voiced his plan to form a broad "national salvation" [[coalition government]] of all parties except the currently governing [[HDZ]]. He also urged voters to vote for anyone except HDZ.<ref>{{cite web |title=Milanović: Izašao sam iz zone komfora i krenuo. Krenite i vi! |url=https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/milanovic-izasao-iz-zone-komfora-i-krenuo-krenite-i-vi-20240413 |website=tportal.hr |publisher=Tportal |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=13 April 2024 |archive-date=13 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413085519/https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/milanovic-izasao-iz-zone-komfora-i-krenuo-krenite-i-vi-20240413 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Milanović poslao poruku biračima: "Glasuj za sve, samo za HDZ* NE!" |url=https://www.novilist.hr/novosti/hrvatska/milanovic-poslao-poruku-biracima-glasuj-za-sve-samo-za-hdz-ne/ |website=novilist.hr |publisher=Novi list |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=12 April 2024 |archive-date=13 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413020834/https://www.novilist.hr/novosti/hrvatska/milanovic-poslao-poruku-biracima-glasuj-za-sve-samo-za-hdz-ne/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[The Bridge (Croatia)|The Bridge]] stated that they will form a government with any party which accepts their program and PM candidate [[Nikola Grmoja]]. Unlike [[Social Democratic Party of Croatia|SDP]], [[We Can! (Croatia)|We Can!]] strongly rejected participating in a government with the Most or DP, saying they are the only barrier to the right in government. In case of a [[gridlock (politics)|gridlock]] in [[government formation]] after the election, they are ready to provide [[confidence and supply]] to an SDP [[minority government]] from Sabor, with the condition that the right does the same and doesn't enter the new cabinet.<ref>{{cite web |title=SDP i Domovinski pokret potencijalni politički partneri? Hajdaš Dončić zaintrigirao izjavom |url=https://www.dnevno.hr/vijesti/sdp-i-domovinski-pokret-kao-potencijalni-politicki-partneri-hajdas-doncic-zaintrigirao-izjavom-2371456/ |website=dnevno.hr |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=27 March 2024 |archive-date=31 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240331051734/https://www.dnevno.hr/vijesti/sdp-i-domovinski-pokret-kao-potencijalni-politicki-partneri-hajdas-doncic-zaintrigirao-izjavom-2371456/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sandra Benčić jasno rekla što će Možemo učiniti ako na izborima dođe do pat pozicije |url=https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/sandra-bencic-jasno-rekla-sto-ce-mozemo-uciniti-ako-na-izborima-dode-do-pat-pozicije-foto-20240411?meta_refresh=1 |website=tportal.hr |publisher=Tportal |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=11 April 2024 |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419203616/https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/sandra-bencic-jasno-rekla-sto-ce-mozemo-uciniti-ako-na-izborima-dode-do-pat-pozicije-foto-20240411?meta_refresh=1 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Ivan Penava]] stated that We Can! and [[Independent Democratic Serb Party|SDSS]] are unacceptable as partners for the [[Homeland Movement (Croatia)|Homeland Movement]], but not SDP.<ref>{{cite web |title=Penava: SDP nam je prihvatljiv, ali Možemo! i SDSS apsolutno nisu |url=https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/penava-sdp-nam-je-prihvatljiv-ali-mozemo-i-sdss-apsolutno-nisu-foto-20240316 |website=tportal.hr |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=16 March 2024 |archive-date=27 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240327225143/https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/penava-sdp-nam-je-prihvatljiv-ali-mozemo-i-sdss-apsolutno-nisu-foto-20240316 |url-status=live }}</ref>

During a campaign rally in [[Split, Croatia|Split]], Andrej Plenković criticized Zoran Milanović, who has espoused [[Zoran Milanović#War in Ukraine|supportive stances on Russia]], for "pushing Croatia and the Croatian people into the ‘[[Russian World]]’". He also compared the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]] to [[Croatian War of Independence|Serbian aggression against Croatia]] in the 1990s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Croatian PM accuses President Milanović of pushing nation towards 'Russian World' |url=https://tvpworld.com/76974828/croatian-pm-accuses-president-milanovic-of-pushing-nation-towards-russian-world |website=TVP World |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=English |date=14 April 2024 |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419203614/https://tvpworld.com/76974828/croatian-pm-accuses-president-milanovic-of-pushing-nation-towards-russian-world |url-status=live }}</ref> The numerous [[political corruption]] scandals within the government have weakened the HDZ campaign. Some thirty ministers have had to leave the government in eight years because of corruption.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 April 2024 |title=Graft scandals threaten conservatives' bid for third term in Croatia election |url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/graft-scandals-threaten-conservatives%27-bid-for-third-term-in-croatia-election/75595381 |access-date= |website=SWI swissinfo.ch |language=en-GB |archive-date=17 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240417225931/https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/graft-scandals-threaten-conservatives%27-bid-for-third-term-in-croatia-election/75595381 |url-status=live }}</ref> The scandal involving private [[WhatsApp]] messages of former HDZ official [[Josipa Rimac]] with the new [[State's Attorney Office of the Republic of Croatia|State Attorney of Croatia]] Ivan Turudić, that were one of the causes of the [[2024 Zagreb protest]], continued during the campaign and this time involved the HDZ [[Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure (Croatia)|Minister of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure]] [[Oleg Butković]]. In April, several previously unreleased sets of leaked messages were published by [[Faktograf.hr]] that apparently testify to some dubious actions and deal-making by Rimac, involving suspicions of [[lobbying]], [[influence peddling]] and [[nepotism]]. Butković denied remembering contacts with Rimac.<ref>{{cite web |title=Faktograf otkriva kako je Josipa Rimac zapošljavala njoj bliske ljude uz pomoć ministra Olega Butkovića |url=https://faktograf.hr/2024/04/04/faktograf-otkriva-kako-je-josipa-rimac-zaposljavala-njoj-bliske-ljude-uz-pomoc-ministra-olega-butkovica/ |website=faktograf.hr |publisher=Faktograf |access-date=19 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=4 April 2024 |archive-date=17 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240417004334/https://faktograf.hr/2024/04/04/faktograf-otkriva-kako-je-josipa-rimac-zaposljavala-njoj-bliske-ljude-uz-pomoc-ministra-olega-butkovica/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Josipa Rimac utjecala je na bivšeg predsjednika DKOM-a Gorana Matešića u korist Večernjeg lista |url=https://faktograf.hr/2024/04/09/josipa-rimac-utjecala-je-na-bivseg-predsjednika-dkom-a-gorana-matesica-u-korist-vecernjeg-lista/ |website=faktograf.hr |publisher=Faktograf |access-date=19 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=9 April 2024 |archive-date=15 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415195803/https://faktograf.hr/2024/04/09/josipa-rimac-utjecala-je-na-bivseg-predsjednika-dkom-a-gorana-matesica-u-korist-vecernjeg-lista/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Butković o prepisci s Josipom Rimac: 'Ja se tih poruka ne sjećam. Kako bih mogao utjecati na zapošljavanje u privatnoj tvrtki?' |url=https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/butkovic-o-prepisci-s-josipom-rimac-ja-se-tih-poruka-ne-sjecam-kako-bih-mogao-utjecati-na-zaposljavanje-u-privatnoj-tvrtki/ |website=telegram.hr |publisher=Telegram |access-date=19 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=5 April 2024 |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419203516/https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/butkovic-o-prepisci-s-josipom-rimac-ja-se-tih-poruka-ne-sjecam-kako-bih-mogao-utjecati-na-zaposljavanje-u-privatnoj-tvrtki/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In the messages, Rimac also criticized the former Conflict of Interest Commission presidents Nataša Novaković and [[Dalija Orešković]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Procurile nove poruke Josipe Rimac. Unlike in [[2016 Croatian parliamentary election|2016]]<ref>{{cite web |title=I udarci ispod pojasa: Žustra debata Milanovića i Plenkovića |url=https://www.24sata.hr/news/uoci-izborne-sutnje-milanovic-i-plenkovic-u-jos-jednoj-debati-490514 |website=24sata.hr |publisher=24sata |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=9 September 2016 |archive-date=18 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230618203932/https://www.24sata.hr/news/uoci-izborne-sutnje-milanovic-i-plenkovic-u-jos-jednoj-debati-490514 |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[2020 Croatian parliamentary election|2020]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Plenković: Ne znate baš ništa, meni je vas iskreno žao, Bernardić: Čini mi se da je dosta bahat |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/veceras-suceljavanje-andreja-plenkovica-i-davora-bernardica-1413336 |website=vecernji.hr |publisher=Večernji list |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=29 June 2020 |archive-date=1 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220301102317/https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/veceras-suceljavanje-andreja-plenkovica-i-davora-bernardica-1413336 |url-status=live }}</ref> the leaders of two biggest parties, HDZ and SDP, did not attend a single [[debate]]. [[Peđa Grbin]] challenged [[Andrej Plenković]] to one, but Plenković refused to debate Grbin, as the PM candidate of [[Rivers of Justice]] is [[Zoran Milanović]]. The [[Prime Minister of Croatia|Prime Minister]] refused to debate other political opponents, saying that he doesn't have anyone to debate with. DP leader [[Ivan Penava]] and PM candidates [[Nikola Grmoja]] (Most) and [[Sandra Benčić]] (Možemo!) also challenged Plenković to a debate. Grbin, Grmoja and Benčić all suggested Plenković is afraid and/or called him a coward.<ref>{{cite web |title=Andrej Plenković: "Nemam se s kim sučeljavati, kršitelj Ustava imao je vremena" |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/andrej-plenkovic-daje-izjave-nakon-sjednice-predsjednistva-hdz-a---841145.html |website=dnevnik.hr |publisher=Nova TV |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=2 April 2024 |archive-date=10 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240410200437/https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/andrej-plenkovic-daje-izjave-nakon-sjednice-predsjednistva-hdz-a---841145.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Grmoja: Plenković se boji sučeljavanja, a želi još četiri godine mandata |url=https://n1info.hr/vijesti/grmoja-plenkovic-se-boji-suceljavanja-a-zeli-jos-cetiri-godine-mandata/ |website=n1info.hr |publisher=N1 |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=12 April 2024 |archive-date=15 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415191130/https://n1info.hr/vijesti/grmoja-plenkovic-se-boji-suceljavanja-a-zeli-jos-cetiri-godine-mandata/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Grbin ponovno Plenkovića pozvao na sučeljavanje: 'Stari moj, pokaži se, ne budi kukavica' |url=https://www.jutarnji.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/grbin-ponovno-plenkovica-pozvao-na-suceljavanje-stari-moj-pokazi-se-ne-budi-kukavica-15449527 |website=jutarnji.hr |publisher=Jutarnji list |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=12 April 2024 |archive-date=12 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240412115621/https://www.jutarnji.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/grbin-ponovno-plenkovica-pozvao-na-suceljavanje-stari-moj-pokazi-se-ne-budi-kukavica-15449527 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Benčić: 'Plenković je kukavica. Ne želi sučeljavanje jer se boji'; Tomašević: 'Vjerujemo u većinu s SDP-om' |url=https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/bencic-plenkovic-je-kukavica-ne-zeli-suceljavanje-jer-se-boji-tomasevic-vjerujemo-u-vecinu-s-sdp-om/ |website=telegram.hr |publisher=Telegram |access-date=14 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=14 April 2024 |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419203619/https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/bencic-plenkovic-je-kukavica-ne-zeli-suceljavanje-jer-se-boji-tomasevic-vjerujemo-u-vecinu-s-sdp-om/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=VIDEO Penava poziva Plenkovića na sučeljavanje: 'Prizemno i šovinistički vrijeđa dijelove hrvatskog naroda' |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/video-penava-poziva-plenkovica-na-suceljavanje-prizemno-i-sovinisticki-vrijeda-dijelove-hrvatskog-naroda-1761613 |website=vecernji.hr |publisher=Večernji list |access-date=14 April 2024 |archive-date=14 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240414202101/https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/video-penava-poziva-plenkovica-na-suceljavanje-prizemno-i-sovinisticki-vrijeda-dijelove-hrvatskog-naroda-1761613 |url-status=live }}</ref> To the calls to debate them, Plenković responded by saying: "This is a political match in which Grbin capitulated before the formal campaign, Milanović violates the Constitution, and a political trifle, like Most, is not someone we would confront (in a debate)." ==Results==
The election produced a fourth consecutive victory for the governing [[HDZ]]; however, the opposition parties denied it a one-party majority in the Sabor. The official results showed that HDZ's coalition won 61 seats, almost 20 seats more than the second placed [[Rivers of Justice]] coalition whose 42 candidates were elected.<ref name="apresult">{{Cite web |date=18 April 2024 |title=Croatia's ruling conservatives win parliamentary vote, but cannot rule alone |url=https://apnews.com/article/croatia-election-european-union-plenkovic-milanovic-b3a93b2598f60ebfdf663815dda2c0ad |work=Associated Press |url-status=live |access-date=18 April 2024 |archive-date=18 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240418044737/https://apnews.com/article/croatia-election-european-union-plenkovic-milanovic-b3a93b2598f60ebfdf663815dda2c0ad }}</ref> Despite HDZ's plurality of votes, in order to form a governing majority, they still required to rely on forming a coalition, with the most likely partners the third-placed far-right party, the [[Homeland Movement (Croatia)|Homeland Movement]], which won 14 seats.<ref name="HR elect 24 US News">{{cite news|url=https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2024-04-17/croatia-votes-in-a-parliamentary-election-thats-a-showdown-between-its-president-and-prime-minister|title=Croatia's Ruling Conservatives Win Parliamentary Vote, but Cannot Rule Alone|publisher=US News|author=[[Associated Press]]|date=17 April 2024|access-date=23 April 2024|archive-date=17 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240417063939/https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2024-04-17/croatia-votes-in-a-parliamentary-election-thats-a-showdown-between-its-president-and-prime-minister|url-status=live}}</ref> The Homeland Movement therefore has the kingmaker position,<ref name="HR elect 24 US News" /> although it declined to say whether they would join a left-leaning or right-leaning bloc and setting the condition that they will not enter into a coalition with [[Independent Democratic Serb Party|SDSS]] and [[We can! (Croatia)|Možemo]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sprečić |first=Elvis |last2=Josipović |first2=Tatjana |last3=Grgin |first3=Matea |date=17 April 2024 |title=Penava dočekan ovacijama: 'SDSS u niti jednoj varijanti i ni pod kojim uvjetima. Ni stranka Možemo' |trans-title=Penava was greeted with a standing ovation: 'SDSS in no variant and under no conditions. Neither the We Can Party' |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/uzivo-iz-stozera-domovinskog-pokreta-1762400 |access-date=25 April 2024 |website=Večernji list |language=hr |archive-date=25 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240425163535/https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/uzivo-iz-stozera-domovinskog-pokreta-1762400 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Among the other opposition parties, conservative [[The Bridge (Croatia)|The Bridge]] along with partners [[Croatian Sovereignists]] won 11 seats, and the green-left [[We can! (Croatia)|We Can!]] who won 10, both declared after the vote they intended to start talks with potential allies aimed at putting together some form of majority administration.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/apr/18/croatia-election-results-hdz-democratic-union-pm-andrej-plenkovic-without-majority-sdp-homeland-movement|date=18 April 2024|title=Political uncertainty in Croatia as ruling party wins most seats but no majority|work=[[The Guardian]]|author=Jon Henley|access-date=23 April 2024|archive-date=22 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240422190025/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/apr/18/croatia-election-results-hdz-democratic-union-pm-andrej-plenkovic-without-majority-sdp-homeland-movement|url-status=live}}</ref> The latter party also encouraged all smaller parties regardless of political leanings to come to an agreement in order to oust HDZ from power. The [[Workers' Front (Croatia)|Workers' Front]] failed to achieve the 5% [[electoral threshold]], leaving the party without a representative in the [[Sabor]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/potop-radnicke-fronte-katarina-peovic-nije-presla-izborni-prag-1762451 |title=Potop Radničke fronte: Katarina Peović nije prešla izborni prag |trans-title=Descent of the Workers' Front: Katarina Peović did not cross the electoral threshold |newspaper=[[Večernji list]] |date=17 April 2024 |access-date=20 April 2024 |archive-date=20 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420100557/https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/potop-radnicke-fronte-katarina-peovic-nije-presla-izborni-prag-1762451 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Aftermath==
[[Andrej Plenković]] claimed victory on behalf of the [[Croatian Democratic Union|HDZ]] and said that it would begin the process of forming a new parliamentary majority to form the HDZ's third government on 18 April 2024. He also congratulated other contesting parties.<ref name="apresult"/> [[Social Democratic Party of Croatia|SDP]] leader [[Peđa Grbin]] said that they had hoped for a better result but said that they would also start talks on the formation of a new government on 18 April.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 April 2024 |title=Ruling HDZ party wins most seats, but no majority in Croatia election |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/4/17/croatia-ruling-party-heading-for-election-win-without-majority-exit-poll |work=Al Jazeera |url-status=live |access-date=18 April 2024 |archive-date=17 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240417210612/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/4/17/croatia-ruling-party-heading-for-election-win-without-majority-exit-poll }}</ref> During negotiation talks, the [[Homeland Movement (Croatia)|DP]] was labeled the kingmaker of the election.<ref>{{cite web |title=Croatia ruling party races to form coalition after election win |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/croatian-ruling-party-wins-polls-prepares-talks-forming-government-2024-04-18/ |website=[[Reuters]] |access-date=19 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Orovic |first1=Joe |last2=Higgins |first2=Andrew |title=A Far-Right Party Emerges as a Possible Kingmaker in Croatia |work=The New York Times |date=18 April 2024 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/04/18/world/europe/croatia-election-far-right.html |access-date=19 April 2024 |archive-date=18 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240418164648/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/04/18/world/europe/croatia-election-far-right.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 19 April, the [[Constitutional Court of Croatia|Constitutional Court]] ruled that President Zoran Milanović was ineligible to become prime minister in the event that the SDP would be able to form a government, citing his statements and behavior during the electoral campaign. According to the ruling, he would be barred from being given the mandate to form a new government even if he previously resigned as President.<ref>{{cite web |title=Croatia's top court rules President Milanović cannot be prime minister because of campaign |url=https://apnews.com/article/croatia-election-president-constitution-milanovic-court-sdp-7cd3da5839c0e641a113a6f9d8b31a08 |website=[[Associated Press]] |date=19 April 2024 |access-date=19 April 2024 |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419204151/https://apnews.com/article/croatia-election-president-constitution-milanovic-court-sdp-7cd3da5839c0e641a113a6f9d8b31a08 |url-status=live }}</ref> Three of the Constitutional Court judges released a [[dissenting opinion]] pointing out there are no specific arguments or regulations to justify the decision. They cited "unconstitutional threats" of the Court and criticized the potential undermining of the will of the people.<ref>{{cite web |title=Troje sudaca protiv odluke o Milanoviću: "Ovo je prijetnja novom Saboru da paze što rade" |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/objavljeno-izdvojeno-misljenje-sudaca-ustavnog-suda---844058.html |website=dnevnik.hr |publisher=Nova TV |access-date=19 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=19 April 2024 |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419204150/https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/objavljeno-izdvojeno-misljenje-sudaca-ustavnog-suda---844058.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Milanović gave a statement in front of a photo showing "HDZ's man" [[Miroslav Šeparović]], the Court's President, hanging out together with HDZ ministers [[Oleg Butković]] and [[Branko Bačić]], accusing the Court of preparing a [[coup d'état]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Milanović šefu Ustavnog suda odgovorio fotografijom: "Pogledajte kako HDZ donosi odluke tzv. Ustavnog suda" |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/zoran-milanovic-najavio-konferenciju-za-novinare-uz-objavu-na-facebooku---844050.html?itm_source=TopNews&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |website=dnevnik.hr |publisher=Nova TV |access-date=19 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=19 April 2024 |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419204349/https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/zoran-milanovic-najavio-konferenciju-za-novinare-uz-objavu-na-facebooku---844050.html?itm_source=TopNews&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Milanović: 'Ovo je priprema za državni udar. Mandatar može biti bilo tko' |url=https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/uskoro-uzivo-milanovic-ce-govoriti-o-odluci-ustavnog-suda-20240419?meta_refresh=1 |website=tportal.hr/ |publisher=Tportal |access-date=19 April 2024 |language=Croatian |date=19 April 2024 |archive-date=22 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240422202330/https://www.tportal.hr/vijesti/clanak/uskoro-uzivo-milanovic-ce-govoriti-o-odluci-ustavnog-suda-20240419?meta_refresh=1 |url-status=live }}</ref>

As one of the scenarios for the formation of a new government, Grbin presented the idea of an anti-corruption government. This would imply the constitution of a Parliament in which, at least temporarily, the majority will be all opposition parties (Možemo!, Rivers of Justice, IDS, Fokus, Most, and DP). Such a parliamentary majority could pass several important laws, including the electoral one, as well as annul the appointment of State Attorney Ivan Turudić. After that, in the event that the parties could not agree on the formation of a joint government, new elections could be held.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Škaro |first=Katarina |date=20 April 2024 |title=Grbin iznio detalje novog plana za Sabor. Beljak, iz koalicije Rijeka pravde, kaže: 'To je znanstvena fantastika' |trans-title=Grbin presented the details of the new plan for the Parliament. Beljak, from the Rivers of Justice coalition, says: 'It's science fiction' |url=https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/grbin-iznio-detalje-novog-plana-za-sabor-beljak-iz-koalicije-rijeka-pravde-kaze-to-je-znanstvena-fantastika/ |access-date=20 April 2024 |website=Telegram |language=hr |archive-date=20 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420150759/https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/grbin-iznio-detalje-novog-plana-za-sabor-beljak-iz-koalicije-rijeka-pravde-kaze-to-je-znanstvena-fantastika/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 21 April, elections were repeated in two polling stations. The first was in [[Sračinec]], where an excess of ballots was found in the ballot boxes. The irregularity referred to the list of candidates in the [[Electoral district XII (Croatian Parliament)|XII electoral unit]] where representatives of the Albanian, Bosniak, Montenegrin, Macedonian and Slovenian national minorities were elected. The second polling station was in [[Markušica]] in the village of [[Ostrovo, Croatia|Ostrovo]], where it was discovered that by mistake 83 persons of Serbian nationality voted twice, namely for the [[Electoral district V (Croatian Parliament)|V electoral unit]] and for the candidates of the XII electoral unit of the Serbian national minority.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vištica |first=Sanja |date=20 April 2024 |title=Ponavljaju se izbori u dva mjesta: Poništeni su zbog velikih nepravilnosti |trans-title=Elections are repeated in two places: They were annulled due to major irregularities |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/gradjani-ce-ponovno-na-izbore-saznajte-zasto-u-prilogu-sanje-vistice---844155.html?itm_source=TopNews&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |access-date=21 April 2024 |website=Dnevnik.hr |language=hr |archive-date=21 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240421112051/https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/gradjani-ce-ponovno-na-izbore-saznajte-zasto-u-prilogu-sanje-vistice---844155.html?itm_source=TopNews&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 27 April, the DP held negotiation talks with both the HDZ and SDP, with Prime Minister [[Andrej Plenković]] announcing that the HDZ would form a formal coalition with the DP some time in "the coming days."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Badovinac |first1=Nikola |title=Homeland Movement meets with HDZ and SDP |url=https://glashrvatske.hrt.hr/en/politics/homeland-movement-meets-with-hdz-and-sdp-11506517 |website=glashrvatske.hrt.hr |access-date=2 May 2024 |archive-date=2 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502125523/https://glashrvatske.hrt.hr/en/politics/homeland-movement-meets-with-hdz-and-sdp-11506517 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 29 April, the State Electoral Commission published the final results, setting a deadline to 19 May for holding the first session of the Sabor with president Milanović deciding the exact date.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 April 2024 |title=Objavljeni su konačni izborni rezultati: Počeo teći važan rok od 20 dana |trans-title=The final election results have been published: An important period of 20 days has begun |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/konacni-izborni-rezultati-parlamentarni-izbori-2024---845518.html?itm_source=SpecialNews&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |access-date=29 April 2024 |website=Dnevnik.hr |language=hr}}</ref>

On 5 May, an agreement was reached on the HDZ and DP government, with Plenković as prime minister. DP will receive three ministries, demography, agriculture, and energy, which will be separated from the Ministry of Economy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2024 |title=Plenković: "Dogovorili smo da tri resora pripadnu DP-u. Prvi u EU uvodimo to ministarstvo" |trans-title=Plenković: "We agreed that three departments belong to the DP. We are the first to introduce that ministry to the EU." |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/andrej-plenkovic-u-jastrebarskom---847133.html?itm_source=TopNews&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |access-date=8 May 2024 |website=Dnevnik.hr |language=hr}}</ref> Members of the [[Serbs of Croatia|Serb community]] were excluded from the new cabinet due to opposition from the DP.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 May 2024 |title=Croatia conservative leader Plenkovic appointed as prime minister-designate for third term |url=https://apnews.com/article/croatia-government-prime-minister-farright-5fe457449cdb83c804f55dad041d5f33 |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> On 10 May Plenković submitted 78 signatures of representatives at a meeting with president Milanović at the [[Presidential Palace, Zagreb|Presidential Palace]], after which Milanović gave him a mandate to form the government. The signatures were given by 61 representatives of the HDZ coalition, 12 representatives of the DP, four representatives of minorities and [[Vesna Vučemilović]], who was subsequently expelled from the Croatian Sovereignists.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 May 2024 |title=Plenković donio potpise za novu Vladu, Milanović se oglasio priopćenjem. Vučemilović izbačena iz Suverenista |trans-title=Plenković brought the signatures for the new Government, Milanović made a statement. Vučemilović expelled from Sovereignist |url=https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/plenkovic-donio-milanovicu-78-potpisa-milic-dobili-smo-mandat-za-sastavljanje-vlade/ |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=Telegram |language=hr}}</ref> The Sabor issued its approval of the new government in a 79–61 vote on 17 May.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 May 2024 |title=Croatia gets new government with a far-right party included ahead of European parliamentary vote |url=https://apnews.com/article/croatia-government-far-right-european-election-240941791de21a8c8a35acb2b2082cde |access-date=18 May 2024 |website=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

|url=https://hungarytoday.hu/mi-hazank-election-result-parliament-2022/ |access-date=4 April 2022 |website=Hungary Today |language=en}} Internationally, the election was seen as a victory for [[right-wing populism]] with Orbán being an ally of then former US President [[Donald Trump]] and other right-wing figures.{{Cite web |date=4 April 2022 |title=Viktor Orbán's win shows there's still hope for Trumpism in Europe |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/think/opinion/putin-war-ukraine-hungary-orban-trump-rcna22881 |access-date=17 September 2024 |website=NBC News |language=en}} ==Background== ===Creation of joint opposition list=== On 8 April 2018, just like in 2010 and 2014, [[Fidesz-KDNP]] won with two-third majority, collecting almost every second votes of people. Following the election, the main opposition parties, which had previously run alone or partly united, gradually realized that Fidesz could only be defeated through full cooperation. The first step of this was a joint demonstration in December of that year against the so called "slave law", which would have required workers to work in overtime.{{cite web|url=https://168.hu/itthon/hosok-tere-tuntetes-2018-12-16-160763|title=Hatalmas tüntetést tartottak a Kossuth téren, több ezer ember vonult az MTVA székházához|date=16 December 2018}} In [[2019 Hungarian local elections|2019 local elections]], [[Democratic Coalition (Hungary)|Democratic Coalition]], [[Jobbik]], [[LMP – Hungary's Green Party]], [[Hungarian Socialist Party]], [[Momentum Movement]], [[Dialogue for Hungary]], and numerous other parties or [[independent candidates]] ran in joint lists. It enabled opposition parties to win the majority in the [[General Assembly of Budapest]] and in ten of the 23 cities with county rights.{{Cite web |title=Helyi önkormányzati választás 2019 - Nemzeti Választási Iroda |url=https://www.valasztas.hu/d4/onk19/szavossz/onkval/hu/kiemelt.html |work=www.valasztas.hu |accessdate=15 October 2019}} On 13 August 2020, the six parties decided to field joint candidates in all of Hungary's 106 constituencies and launch a joint program for the elections,{{cite web|url=https://hungarytoday.hu/opposition-to-field-joint-candidates-in-all-constituencies-in-2022/|title=Opposition to Field Joint Candidates in All Constituencies in 2022|date=14 August 2020}} later agreed on running with a common candidate for [[Prime Minister of Hungary|Prime Minister]], to be selected in a primary election. They expected the candidate to be selected by 23 October 2021.[https://telex.hu/belfold/2020/11/16/kozos-miniszterelnok-jeloltet-allitanak-az-ellenzeki-partok-2022-re Közös miniszterelnök-jelöltet állítanak az ellenzéki pártok 2022-re], ''telex.hu'' (in Hungarian) On 20 December 2020, DK, Jobbik, Momentum, MSZP, LMP and Dialogue decided on running together on a [[United for Hungary|common list]], solidifying their electoral alliance.{{Cite web|date=20 December 2020|title=Megszületett a teljes ellenzéki összefogás|url=https://m.hvg.hu/itthon/20201220_Megszuletett_a_teljes_ellenzeki_osszefogas|access-date=23 December 2020|website=hvg.hu|language=hu}}{{Cite web|first1=Lili|last1=Bayer|date=20 December 2020|title=Hungarian opposition unites in bid to unseat Viktor Orbán|url=https://www.politico.eu/article/hungary-opposition-unites-in-bid-to-unseat-orban/|access-date=23 December 2020|website=POLITICO|language=en-US}} The leaders of the respective parties have also signed a declaration containing the terms of their cooperation, titled "Korszakváltás Garanciái" (Principles for Hungary's governance after 2022"). The opposition coalition was very ideologically diverse, something described by observers as a potential hindrance to presenting a united front to defeat Orbán.{{cite web | last1=Bayer | first1=Lili | title=Inside the Hungarian campaign to beat Viktor Orbán | url=https://www.politico.eu/article/inside-the-hungarian-opposition-uphill-battle-to-beat-viktor-orban-fidesz-party/ | date=26 July 2021 | work=[[Politico]] | access-date=31 July 2021}} ===Amendment of the electoral law=== The electoral law, under which the previous two elections were held ([[2014 Hungarian parliamentary election|2014]] and [[2018 Hungarian parliamentary election|2018]]), specified the number of constituency candidates a party needed to run nationwide at 27, in at least 9 counties. On 15 December 2020, the National Assembly, in which the governing parties held the needed a two-third majority, voted to increase the requirements to a total of 71 constituency candidates in at least 14 counties and the [[Budapest|capital]].{{Cite web|title=2011. évi CCIII. törvény az országgyűlési képviselők választásáról|trans-title=Act CCIII. of 2011. on the election of members of the National Assembly|url=https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a1100203.tv|url-status=live|language=hu|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915122359/https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=A1100203.TV |archive-date=15 September 2018 }}{{Cite web|title=Megszavazták a választási törvény és az alaptörvény módosítását is|date=15 December 2020|url=https://24.hu/belfold/2020/12/15/alaptorveny-alkotmany-szavazas-parlament/|url-status=live|language=hu|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201215113318/https://24.hu/belfold/2020/12/15/alaptorveny-alkotmany-szavazas-parlament/ |archive-date=15 December 2020 }} ===Opposition primary=== {{Main|2021 Hungarian opposition primary}} The [[United for Hungary|Opposition]] primary was held in [[Hungary]], between 12 and 27 September 2021 (first round) and 10–16 October 2021 (second round), to select the candidate for Prime Minister supported by the opposition parties to form a coalition to compete in the 2022 Hungarian parliamentary election. It was the first countrywide primary election in the political history of Hungary. On 17 October 2021, non-partisan candidate [[Péter Márki-Zay]] won in the runoff (second round) of the opposition primary, becoming the [[United for Hungary|United Opposition]] candidate in the election for prime minister. The parties had also selected common candidates for [[single-member district]]s via the primary in the first round.{{cite news |last=Bayer |first=Lili |date=17 October 2021 |title=Conservative wins Hungarian opposition race to face Orbán in 2022 |work=Politico |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/conservative-peter-marki-zay-wins-hungary-opposition-race-to-face-viktor-orban-in-2022/}} ==Electoral system== {{Main|Electoral system of Hungary}} The 199 members of the [[National Assembly (Hungary)|National Assembly]] are to be elected by [[mixed-member majoritarian representation]] with two methods; 106 are elected in single-member constituencies by [[first-past-the-post voting]], with the remaining 93 elected from a single nationwide constituency mostly by [[proportional representation]], via a [[Scorporo|partially compensatory system]] (a hybrid of [[parallel voting]] and [[mixed single vote]]). The electoral threshold is set at 5%, although this is raised to 10% for coalitions of two parties and 15% for coalitions of three or more parties. Seats are allocated using the [[d'Hondt method]].[http://www.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2141_B.htm Electoral system] IPU The governing party is allowed to draw the boundaries of the single-member constituencies, and the boundaries were gerrymandered by the Fidesz government prior to the 2014 elections. The redrawing was done in a way that smaller constituencies (with fewer than 70,000 voters) had higher concentrations of Fidesz voters than larger constituencies (over 80,000 voters), meaning fewer votes were required to elect Fidesz constituency candidates.[https://www.economist.com/graphic-detail/2022/04/02/a-wild-gerrymander-makes-hungarys-fidesz-party-hard-to-dislodge A wild gerrymander makes Hungary’s Fidesz party hard to dislodge] The Economist, 2 April 2022 In 2010, seats varied in population by 35%.{{Cite web |title=Ezért érhet kevesebbet az ellenzéki szavazat, mint a Fideszre adott – választásföldrajzi gyorstalpaló {{!}} Válasz Online |url=https://www.valaszonline.hu/2022/01/18/valasztasi-foldrajz-keruletek-lakossag-aranytalansag-elemzes/ |access-date=2023-04-15 |language=hu}} Since 2014 each of the [[Armenians in Hungary|Armenian]], [[Bulgarians in Hungary|Bulgarian]], [[Croats of Hungary|Croatian]], [[Germans of Hungary|German]], [[Greeks in Hungary|Greek]], [[Poles in Hungary|Polish]], [[Romani people in Hungary|Romani]], [[Romanians in Hungary|Romanian]], [[Rusyns|Rusyn]], [[Serbs of Hungary|Serbian]], [[Slovaks in Hungary|Slovak]], [[Hungarian Slovenes|Slovenian]], and [[Ukrainians in Hungary|Ukrainian]] ethnic minorities can win one of the 93 party lists seats if they register as a specific list and reach a lowered quota of \frac{1}{4 \times 93}=\frac{1}{372}\approx0.2688\% of the total of party list votes. Each minority is able to send a minority spokesman – without the rights of an MP – to the National Assembly, if the list does not reach this lowered quota.[http://www.valasztas.hu/web/national-election-office/parliamentary-elections-2018 Nemzeti Választási Iroda] National Election Office Due to internal disputes, the National Self-Government of Romani did not participate in the election.{{cite news |last1=Kaufmann |first1=Balázs |title=Botrányos közgyűlés után nemzetiségi lista nélkül maradt az Országos Roma Önkormányzat |url=https://444.hu/2022/02/01/botranyos-kozgyules-utan-nemzetisegi-lista-nelkul-maradt-az-orszagos-roma-onkormanyzat |access-date=11 April 2022 |work=444.hu}} ==Parties and coalitions== The following parties were represented in the National Assembly, or have commonly included in public opinion polling: {| class=wikitable ! rowspan=2 colspan=4| Party/Coalition
