On 19 July, the National Assembly convened for a second time to elect a new prime minister.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olarn |first=Helen Regan, Kocha |date=2023-07-13 |title=Critical moment for Thai democracy as parliament fails to elect new prime minister |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/07/12/asia/thailand-parliament-prime-ministerial-vote-intl-hnk/index.html |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> That day, the Constitutional Court unanimously voted to accept a case against Pita regarding his inherited shares of the defunct iTV. They also voted 7–2 to suspend him from MP duty until it reached a ruling, though this did not preclude him from being nominated for prime minister.<ref>{{cite news|title=Charter court suspends Pita|date=19 July 2023|work=Bangkok Post|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2614193/charter-court-suspends-pita|access-date=19 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ives |first=Mike |date=2023-07-19 |title=An Anxious Thailand Awaits a New Leader: Here's What to Know |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/19/world/asia/pita-limjaroenrat-prime-minister-thailand.html |access-date=2023-07-19 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-19 |title=Thai court suspends prime minister hopeful Pita's lawmaker status after his reformist party swept elections |url=https://news.yahoo.com/thai-court-suspends-prime-ministerial-052225282.html |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref> In the subsequent debate, the National Assembly voted against considering him for another round of voting for prime minister.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news |date=2023-07-19 |title=Thai Parliament Bars Election Winner From Running for PM Post |language=en |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-07-19/thai-parliament-bars-election-winner-from-running-for-pm-post |access-date=2023-07-19}}</ref> His renomination was argued to have been against a parliamentary rule prohibiting a repeat motion.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Mike|last1=Ives|first2=Muktita|last2=Suhartono|title=Protesters Gather in Thailand as Parliament Faces Gridlock|date=19 July 2023|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/19/world/asia/pita-limjaroenrat-prime-minister-thailand.html|access-date=20 July 2023}}</ref><ref name=bp_19072023>{{cite news|title=Parliament rejects Pita's renomination for PM|date=19 July 2023|work=The Bangkok Post|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2614294/parliament-rejects-pitas-renomination-for-pm|access-date=20 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Thai parliament rejects Pita's PM nomination |url=https://www.dw.com/en/thai-parliament-rejects-pitas-pm-nomination/a-66280247 |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=dw.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="auto1"/> In the voting for his renomination, 312 voters supported, 394 rejected—most of which were senators—eight abstained and one did not vote.<ref name=bp_19072023/> The decision to prohibit renominations was controversial, with critics arguing that it was unconstitutional. Many complaints were filed to the [[Ombudsmen (Thailand)|Office of the Ombudsman]], which on 24 July agreed to forward the case to the Constitutional Court.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Sattaburuth |first1=Aekarach |title=Parliament vote for PM postponed indefinitely |work=Bangkok Post |date=25 July 2023 |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2617559/parliament-vote-for-pm-postponed-indefinitely |access-date=2023-07-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Ombudsman asks court to postpone PM vote |work=Bangkok Post |date=24 July 2023 |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2616894/ombudsman-asks-court-to-postpone-pm-vote |access-date=2023-07-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Rejection of Pita's renomination as PM 'unconstitutional' : Ombudsman |url=https://www.thaipbsworld.com/thai-ombudsman-asks-the-charter-court-to-suspend-pm-selection-process/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=Thai PBS World |date=24 July 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref> This led to further prime ministerial voting being postponed by Parliament; the next vote had originally been scheduled for 27 July.

===<span class="anchor" id="Pheu Thai-led coalition"></span>Pheu Thai–led coalition===
After Move Forward's attempts were blocked, the opportunity to lead the government formation was passed on to Pheu Thai, who were expected to nominate [[Srettha Thavisin]] to be prime minister.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-07-19 |title=Thai Parliament to Vote for PM Again on July 27 |language=en |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-07-19/thai-parliament-to-vote-for-pm-again-on-july-27-house-speaker |access-date=2023-07-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Pheu Thai to seek support from Senate, other parties |work=Bangkok Post |date=21 July 2023 |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2615487/pheu-thai-to-seek-support-from-senate-other-parties |access-date=2023-07-21}}</ref> As part of Pheu Thai's attempts to form a government, talks were held with many of the conservative and/or pro-junta parties, who insisted that they would not support any coalition including Move Forward due to its policy on amending the [[Lèse-majesté in Thailand|lèse-majesté laws]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thailand's Pheu Thai courts conservative parties |url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics/Thai-election/Thailand-s-Pheu-Thai-courts-conservative-parties |access-date=2023-07-29 |website=Nikkei Asia |language=en-GB}}</ref> This, coupled with an announcement that exiled former prime minister [[Thaksin Shinawatra]] would return to Thailand, fuelled speculations of a deal with outgoing coalition parties that would see Pheu Thai abandoning the coalition with Move Forward.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parpart |first=Erich |date=2023-07-27 |title=Leaders' Meeting in Hong Kong Sparks Speculation on Government Formation and Thaksin's Return to Thailand - Thai Enquirer Current Affairs |url=https://www.thaienquirer.com/50301/leaders-meeting-in-hong-kong-sparks-speculation-on-government-formation-and-thaksins-return-to-thailand/ |access-date=2023-07-29 |website=Thai Enquirer |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Thaksin's pending return signals done deal? |url=https://www.thaipbsworld.com/thaksins-pending-return-signals-done-deal/ |access-date=2023-07-29 |website=Thai PBS World |date=28 July 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 2 August, Pheu Thai announced that it was leaving the eight-party coalition and would attempt to form a new coalition that excludes Move Forward, with Srettha as the candidate for prime minister. On 3 August, the Constitutional Court announced that its decision on Pita's renomination would be made on 16 August. In response, the PM vote, scheduled for 4 August, was again postponed to 22 August.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thepgumpanat |first=Panarat |date=2023-08-03 |title=Vote for Thai PM postponed, uncertainty prolonged |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/thai-alliance-reaffirms-backing-pitas-pm-bid-2023-07-17/ |access-date=2023-08-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Vote for PM postponed |work=Bangkok Post |date=3 August 2023 |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2622895/vote-for-pm-postponed |access-date=2023-08-03}}</ref>

On 7 August, Pheu Thai and Bhumjaithai announced an alliance that would try to form a new coalition government.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thailand's Pheu Thai forms new coalition with third-largest party |url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics/Thai-election/Thailand-s-Pheu-Thai-forms-new-coalition-with-third-largest-party |access-date=2023-08-07 |website=Nikkei Asia |language=en-GB}}</ref> They were joined by six parties—Prachachart, Pheu Thai Ruam Palang, Chart Pattana Kla, Thai Liberal, New Social Power, and the Party of Thai Counties—on 9 August, followed by Chart Thai Pattana on 10 August, bringing their total to 238 MPs, which is less than the initial opposition coalition but which was seen as more favorable to the conservative military establishment in the Senate.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-08-09 |title=Pheu Thai brings 6 small parties into its alliance |work=Bangkok Post |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2626294/pheu-thai-brings-6-small-parties-into-its-alliance |access-date=2023-08-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Thailand's Pheu Thai Party Welcomes New Parties Into Potential Governing Coalition |url=https://thediplomat.com/2023/08/thailands-pheu-thai-party-welcomes-new-parties-into-potential-governing-coalition/ |access-date=2023-08-10 |website=The Diplomat |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 16 August, the Constitutional Court dismissed the petitions on Pita's renomination, stating that the plaintiff was not the directly affected party, clearing the way for a new round of prime ministerial voting.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parpart |first=Erich |date=2023-08-16 |title=Constitutional Court dismisses Move Forward Party's petition, clearing path for the next prime ministerial voting - Thai Enquirer Current Affairs |url=https://www.thaienquirer.com/50433/constitutional-court-dismisses-move-forward-partys-petition-clearing-path-for-the-next-prime-ministerial-voting/ |access-date=2023-08-16 |website=Thai Enquirer |language=en-US}}</ref> An eleven-party coalition was announced on 21 August, including the aforementioned parties along with the military-associated parties United Thai Nation and Palang Pracharath for a total of 314 MPs.<ref name=":3" /> Pheu Thai's alliance with the military parties was controversial among many voters, including some of its own supporters, as its leaders had promised not to join with them before the election.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ratcliffe |first=Rebecca |date=2023-08-21 |title=Thai party of Thaksin Shinawatra strikes deal with ex-military rivals |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/aug/21/pheu-thai-party-thaksin-shinawatra-deal-ex-military-rivals |access-date=2023-08-21 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

A poll published by [[National Institute of Development Administration|NIDA]] the day prior showed that around 64% of those surveyed opposed Pheu Thai allying with military-backed parties.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Thailand's Pheu Thai allies with military rivals to form new government |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/8/21/thailands-pheu-thai-to-ally-with-military-rivals-to-form-new-government |access-date=2023-08-21 |website=www.aljazeera.com |language=en}}</ref> On 22 August at 9{{Nbsp}}am Bangkok time, Thaksin returned to Thailand and landed at [[Don Mueang International Airport]], following 15 years of self-imposed exile, and was promptly sent to court and then prison to begin serving an eight-year sentence for his outstanding corruption convictions.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ratcliffe |first1=Rebecca |last2=Siradapuvadol |first2=Navaon |title=Thaksin Shinawatra jailed on return to Thailand as his party regains power |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/aug/22/thaksin-shinawatra-anger-and-anticipation-in-thailand-as-exiled-former-pm-expected-to-return |access-date=22 August 2023 |work=The Guardian |date=22 August 2023}}</ref> Hours later, he was transferred to the [[Police General Hospital]], which prompted accusations of special treatment.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-29 |title=Daughter of ex-Thai leader Thaksin says he is fatigued, as criticism grows of his hospitalization |url=https://apnews.com/article/thailand-thaksin-shinawatra-hospital-paetongtarn-8e866a52fede6554112955275225dfa0 |access-date=2023-08-31 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> On 31 August, outgoing Justice Minister [[Wissanu Krea-ngam]] confirmed that Thaksin had requested a royal pardon,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-08-31 |title=Thailand's billionaire ex-PM Thaksin submits royal pardon request - media |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/thailands-ex-pm-thaksin-has-submitted-request-royal-pardon-media-2023-08-31/ |access-date=2023-08-31}}</ref> and on 1 September the [[Royal Gazette (Thailand)|Royal Gazette]] announced the King had commuted his sentence to one year.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-09-01 |title=Thai king reduces former PM Thaksin's prison sentence to one year |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/thai-king-reduces-former-pm-thaksins-prison-sentence-one-year-2023-09-01/ |access-date=2023-09-01}}</ref>

On the evening of 22 August, the day of Thaksin's arrival, Srettha Thavisin was elected with 482 votes for, 165 votes against, with 81 abstentions.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Parliament elects Srettha prime minister |language=en |work=Bangkok Post |date=22 August 2023 |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2633946/parliament-elects-srettha-prime-minister |access-date=2023-08-22}}</ref> On 23 August, the King formally endorsed Srettha to become the 30th Prime Minister of Thailand.<ref>{{Cite news |date=23 August 2023 |title=Srettha endorsed by king as Thailand's new PM – official |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/srettha-endorsed-by-king-thailands-new-pm-official-2023-08-23/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |archive-date=23 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230823135310/https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/srettha-endorsed-by-king-thailands-new-pm-official-2023-08-23/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The endorsement document was posted on the Royal Gazette's website.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ratchakitcha |title=พระบรมราชโองการ ประกาศ แต่งตั้งนายกรัฐมนตรี [นายเศรษฐา ทวีสิน] |url=https://ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/documents/140D201S0000000000100.pdf |url-status=live |access-date=23 August 2023 |archive-date=23 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230823132500/https://ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/documents/140D201S0000000000100.pdf }}</ref> At the event, Srettha also gave his first speech as prime minister.<ref>{{Citation |title="เศรษฐา ทวีสิน" รับสนองพระบรมราชโองการ แต่งตั้ง เป็นนายกฯคนที่ 30 ของไทยแล้ว | date=23 August 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IzoK_p279kg |access-date=23 August 2023 |language=en |archive-date=23 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230823135553/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IzoK_p279kg |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Srettha cabinet|His cabinet]] was sworn in on 5 September.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-09-05 |title=Thailand's king swears in new PM and cabinet |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/thailands-king-swears-new-pm-cabinet-2023-09-05/ |access-date=2023-09-08}}</ref>

The protracted government formation led to a further issue: Move Forward had now become the largest opposition party, but one of its MPs, [[Padipat Suntiphada]], had already been elected deputy house speaker by the eight-party coalition. Constitutionally, the opposition leader could not be from the same party as a speaker or deputy speaker. As a result, Move Forward strategically expelled Padipat so that the leadership of the opposition could be taken by its new leader [[Chaithawat Tulathon]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=In a tactical move, Move Forward party sacks Padipat |url=https://www.thaipbsworld.com/in-a-tactical-move-move-forward-party-sacks-padipat/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Thai PBS World |date=29 September 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref> Government parties criticized the expulsion as an undignified political gambit that would in practice keep both positions in Move Forward's control,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Move Forward's expulsion of Padipat slammed as shameful |url=https://www.thaipbsworld.com/move-forwards-expulsion-of-padipat-slammed-as-shameful/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Thai PBS World |date=29 September 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref> while Padipat insisted he would not act as Move Forward's nominee.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Padipat shrugs off criticism over 'expulsion' |language=en |work=Bangkok Post |date=29 September 2023 |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2654871/padipat-shrugs-off-criticism-over-expulsion |access-date=2023-10-01}}</ref>

Voter turnout in the first round was just 11.22 percent,{{cite web | url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20221219-tunisia-election-board-edges-vote-turnout-up-to-11-percent | title=Tunisia election board edges vote turnout up to 11 percent | date=19 December 2022 }} as the election was boycotted by most opposition parties.{{Cite news |date=2022-12-18 |title=Tunisia: President Saied urged to resign after 'fiasco' election |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-64015596 |access-date=2022-12-18}} == Background == {{See also|2021–2022 Tunisian political crisis|2022 Tunisian constitutional referendum}}On 25 July 2021, [[Republic Day (Tunisia)|Republic Day]], after months of [[2021–2022 Tunisian political crisis|political crisis]] between the [[President of Tunisia|President of the Republic]] and [[Assembly of the Representatives of the People]], thousands of demonstrators rallied to call for the dissolution of the Assembly and regime change.{{Cite news |date=2021-07-25 |title=En Tunisie, des milliers de manifestants défilent contre leurs dirigeants |language=fr |work=Le Temps |url=https://www.letemps.ch/monde/tunisie-milliers-manifestants-defilent-contre-leurs-dirigeants |access-date=2022-11-30 |issn=1423-3967}} These rallies are taking place as the health crisis around the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia|COVID-19 pandemic]] escalates. On the same day, President [[Kais Saied]] dismissed the government of [[Hichem Mechichi]] and suspended the activities of the Assembly, using the emergency powers provided for in article 80 of the [[Constitution of Tunisia]].{{Cite web |title=Kais Saied prend tous les pouvoirs en main, suspend le parlement, limoge Mechichi et s'érige en chef de l'exécutif et du parquet |url=https://www.leaders.com.tn/article/32197-kais-saied-prend-tous-les-pouvoirs-en-main-suspend-le-parlement-limoge-mechichi-et-s-erige-en-chef-de-l-executif-et-du-parquet |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Leaders |language=fr}} The country's largest parliamentary party, [[Ennahda]], and its leader, [[Speaker of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People|Assembly Speaker]] [[Rached Ghannouchi]], condemned the president's actions, calling them a [[coup d'état]].{{Cite web |last1=à 00h32 |first1=Par Le Parisien avec AFP Le 26 juillet 2021 |last2=À 11h06 |first2=Modifié Le 26 Juillet 2021 |date=2021-07-25 |title=Tunisie : le président s'arroge le pouvoir exécutif, Ennahdha condamne un "coup d'Etat contre la révolution" |url=https://www.leparisien.fr/international/tunisie-le-president-sarroge-le-pouvoir-executif-ennahdha-condamne-un-coup-detat-contre-la-revolution-26-07-2021-5QRDP25NJJA5NHFEYDXZJ6TTK4.php |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=leparisien.fr |language=fr-FR}} Some political analysts and lawyers have also called the events a coup d'état.{{Cite web |date=2021-07-26 |title=En Tunisie, la crise politique débouche sur une crise constitutionnelle |url=https://www.lesechos.fr/monde/afrique-moyen-orient/en-tunisie-la-crise-politique-debouche-sur-une-crise-constitutionnelle-1334809 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Les Echos |language=fr}} On 22 September, Saied confirmed by decree the extension of the validity of the decisions, as well as the dissolution of the {{Ill|Provisional Body Responsible for Checking the Constitutionality of Bills|fr|Instance provisoire chargée du contrôle de la constitutionnalité des projets de loi}}, and decided to suspend the payment of wages and benefits provided to the chairman of the Assembly of Representatives of the People and its members,{{Cite web |title=Publication de dispositions exceptionnelles de la présidence |url=https://www.mosaiquefm.net/fr/actualite-national-tunisie/962219/publication-de-dispositions-exceptionnelles-de-la-presidence |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=RadioMosaiqueFM |date=22 September 2021 |language=fr}} and granted himself the right to rule by decree, de facto restoring legislative power.{{Cite web |date=2021-09-22 |title=Tunisie : Kaïs Saïed renforce les pouvoirs de la présidence |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/international/tunisie-kais-saied-renforce-les-pouvoirs-de-la-presidence-20210922 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=LEFIGARO |language=fr}} His decision was criticized by most of the parties represented in Parliament.{{Cite web |date=2021-09-23 |title=Tunisie: mécontentement dans la classe politique après les annonces de Kaïs Saïed |url=https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20210923-tunisie-m%C3%A9contentement-dans-la-classe-politique-apr%C3%A8s-les-annonces-de-ka%C3%AFs-sa%C3%AFed |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=RFI |language=fr}} On 29 September, the President instructed [[Najla Bouden]] to form a new [[Bouden Cabinet|government]]. Thus, she became the first female [[Prime Minister of Tunisia|head of government]] in the country and throughout the [[Arab world]].{{Cite web |date=2021-09-29 |title=Tunisie : Najla Bouden Romdhane chargée de former un nouveau gouvernement |url=https://www.france24.com/fr/info-en-continu/20210929-tunisie-najla-bouden-romdhane-charg%C3%A9e-de-former-un-nouveau-gouvernement-officiel |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=France 24 |language=fr}} From 15 January to 20 March 2022, an [[Electronic voting|electronic consultation]] took place on the reforms to be proposed in anticipation of the [[2022 Tunisian constitutional referendum|referendum]]. During the ballot, which was the subject of a very low turnout, the options of a transition to a presidential system and to a single-member ballot for the legislative elections prevailed.{{Cite web |date=2022-03-18 |title=Tunisie : la consultation citoyenne du président Kaïs Saïed a du plomb dans l'aile |url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/franceculture/podcasts/la-revue-de-presse-internationale/la-revue-de-presse-internationale-du-vendredi-18-mars-2022-4842018 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=France Culture |language=fr}}{{Cite web |date=2022-04-01 |title=Tunisie : une consultation largement boudée plébiscite un régime présidentiel |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/flash-actu/tunisie-une-consultation-largement-boudee-plebiscite-un-regime-presidentiel-20220401 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=LEFIGARO |language=fr}}{{Cite web |date=2022-03-22 |title=Tunisie: échec de la consultation nationale en ligne voulue par le président Saïed |url=https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20220322-tunisie-%C3%A9chec-de-la-consultation-nationale-en-ligne-voulue-par-le-pr%C3%A9sident-sa%C3%AFed |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=RFI |language=fr}} On 30 March 2022, 120 deputies, under the chairmanship of the second vice-president of the Assembly Tarek Fetiti,{{Cite web |last=Chamsi |first=Chahrazed |date=2022-03-31 |title=Ftiti: Leur but était de pousser le chef de l'Etat à organiser un dialogue national ou à dissoudre le Parlement [Audio] |url=https://www.tunisienumerique.com/ftiti-leur-but-etait-de-pousser-le-chef-de-letat-a-organiser-un-dialogue-national-ou-a-dissoudre-le-parlement-audio/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Tunisie |language=fr-FR}} met in a virtual session to vote for the end of the exceptional measures in force since 25 July. The same day, Kaïs Saïed dissolved Parliament, which the Constitution forbids during the period when the state of exception is applied, and threatens the deputies with legal proceedings.{{Cite web |date=2022-03-30 |title=Tunisie : la crise institutionnelle s'aggrave |url=https://www.lesechos.fr/monde/afrique-moyen-orient/tunisie-le-president-dissout-le-parlement-1397321 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Les Echos |language=fr}}{{Cite web |title=Tunisie : poussé dans ses derniers retranchements, Kaïs Saïed dissout l'Assemblée – Jeune Afrique |url=https://www.jeuneafrique.com/1334874/politique/tunisie-pousse-dans-ses-derniers-retranchements-kais-saied-dissout-lasssemblee/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=JeuneAfrique.com |date=31 March 2022 |language=fr-FR}} On 6 April, [[Kais Saied]] announced the holding of the parliamentary ballot according to a [[Two-round system|two-round uninominal majority]] ballot.{{Cite news |date=6 April 2022|title=Tunisie: Saïed annonce des nouvelles règles de vote aux élections législatives |url=https://www.challenges.fr/monde/tunisie-saied-annonce-des-nouvelles-regles-de-vote-aux-elections-legislatives_808090 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Challenges |language=fr}} On 5 September, he announced that the electoral law will be drafted taking into consideration the recommendations of the supporters of the 25 July process, and that the rest of the political class will be excluded from this process.{{Cite web |title=Législatives: Un nouveau projet avec les ''adhérents au 25 juillet'' |url=https://www.mosaiquefm.net/fr/actualite-national-tunisie/1083066/legislatives-un-nouveau-projet-avec-les-adherents-au-25-juillet |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=RadioMosaiqueFM |date=5 September 2022 |language=fr}} The electoral law will have to be published no later than 16 September to meet the deadlines. On 25 July 2022, the new Constitution was adopted by [[2022 Tunisian constitutional referendum|constitutional referendum]] with 94.6% of the votes and a 30.5% turnout.{{Cite web |date=2022-07-26 |title=Référendum en Tunisie : la nouvelle Constitution adoptée malgré une forte abstention |url=https://www.france24.com/fr/afrique/20220726-r%C3%A9f%C3%A9rendum-en-tunisie-la-nouvelle-constitution-adopt%C3%A9e-%C3%A0-plus-de-94 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=France 24 |language=fr}} A new electoral law was then published by decree on 15 September.{{Cite web |date=2022-09-15 |title=En Tunisie, une nouvelle loi électorale réduit le rôle des partis politiques |url=https://www.france24.com/fr/afrique/20220915-en-tunisie-une-nouvelle-loi-%C3%A9lectorale-r%C3%A9duit-l-influence-des-partis-politiques |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=France 24 |language=fr}} == Electoral system == The 217 members of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People were previously elected by [[closed list]] [[proportional representation]] in 33 multi-member constituencies (27 in Tunisia and 6 representing Tunisian expatriates) with seats allocated using the [[largest remainder method]] and a mandated [[zipper system]]: alternating female and male candidates on the list, and a male and female candidate under the age of 35 in the top four in constituencies with four or more seats.{{cite web |title=Elections: Tunisia Parliament 2019 |url=https://www.electionguide.org/elections/id/3175/ |website=IFES Election Guide |access-date=6 September 2021}} However, on 16 September 2022, President [[Kais Saied]] introduced a new electoral system and reduced the number of parliamentarians. In this election, the reduced 161 members of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People (now the lower house of a bicameral legislature) will be elected via the [[two-round system]] in single-member constituencies. Additionally, [[publicly funded elections]] were abolished, meaning private support and self-financing must be used, and the law introduced recall referendums, which can be triggered if signatures equal to 10% voters who voted for them submit a request in favor of one to the parliament.{{Cite web |date=2022-09-17 |title=Tunisian president makes new changes to electoral law |url=https://arab.news/ygqqn |access-date=2022-09-20 |website=Arab News |language=en}} Party affiliation of the candidates will no longer appear on ballots. == Campaign == === Procedure === The ISIE publishes the electoral calendar on 23 September 2022.{{Cite web |date=2022-09-24 |title=Tunisie : Le calendrier électoral des législatives publié dans le JORT |url=https://www.webdo.tn/fr/actualite/national/tunisie-le-calendrier-electoral-des-legislatives-publie-dans-le-jort/131043 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=www.webdo.tn |language=fr}} In accordance with the decree of 15 September calling on voters to elect the members of the Assembly of People's Representatives,{{Cite web |date=2022-09-16 |title=Tunisie : Parution du décret appelant les électeurs à élire les membres de l'Assemblée |url=https://news.gnet.tn/tunisie-parution-du-decret-appelant-les-electeurs-a-elire-les-membres-de-lassemblee/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Gnet news |language=fr-FR}} the date of the legislative elections is set for 17 December 2022 on national territory, and from 15 to 17 December abroad. Automatic registration of voters who turn 18 before 16 December is carried out from 21 September.{{Cite web |title=Tunisie: démarrage de l'inscription automatique des électeurs pour les législatives |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/fr/afrique/tunisie-démarrage-de-l-inscription-automatique-des-électeurs-pour-les-législatives/2692572 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=www.aa.com.tr}} The electoral period begins on 25 September at midnight, when it is forbidden to broadcast and publish the results of opinion polls related to the elections.{{Cite web |date=2022-09-25 |title=Tunisie : démarrage de la période électorale pour les législatives |url=https://kapitalis.com/tunisie/2022/09/25/tunisie-demarrage-de-la-periode-electorale-pour-les-legislatives/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Kapitalis |language=fr-FR}} The updating of those registered in the electoral register as well as the change of polling stations take place from 26 September to 13 October.{{Cite web |title=Législatives 2022: Démarrage de l'opération d'actualisation des bureaux de vote |url=http://www.jawharafm.net/fr/article/legislatives-2022-demarrage-de-loperation-dactualisation-des-bureaux-de-vote/90/83119 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=JawharaFM}} The final list of voters is published on 14 October, after the receipt of appeals against the preliminary lists on 29 and 30 September, examined on 1 and 2 October. The submission of applications is open from 17 October to 24 October. They are studied by the ISIE on 13 October to publish the next day, 1 November, the list of candidates on the premises of the ISIE. The final list of candidates is announced on 21 November. The election campaign begins on 25 November. It ends on 13 December abroad and 15 December on national territory, respective dates after which the electoral silence begins. The preliminary results are announced on 20 December, and the final results on 19 January 2023. === Boycott === The [[National Salvation Front (Tunisia)|National Salvation Front]], chaired by [[Ahmed Najib Chebbi]], announced that it was boycotting the legislative election, comparing it to the elections that were held under President [[Zine El Abidine Ben Ali]].{{Cite news |title=Le Front du salut national boycotte les législatives |url=https://www.mosaiquefm.net/fr/actualite-politique-tunisie/1083558/le-front-du-salut-national-boycotte-les-legislatives |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=RadioMosaiqueFM |language=fr}} This coalition, which had also boycotted the constitutional referendum,{{Cite web |date=2022-07-11 |title=Tunisie : le Front du salut réitère son appel au boycott du référendum constitutionnel |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/flash-actu/tunisie-le-front-du-salut-reitere-son-appel-au-boycott-du-referendum-constitutionnel-20220711 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=LEFIGARO |language=fr}} is made up of several political parties including [[Ennahda]], [[Al Amal (political party)|Al Amal]], [[Dignity Coalition]], [[Heart of Tunisia]], [[Movement Party Party (Tunisia)|Republican Party]], [[Democratic Current]], [[Workers' Party (Tunisia)|Workers' Party]] and the [[Democratic Modernist Pole]] also announced its boycott of the election.{{Cite web |date=2022-09-19 |title=Tunisie : Une coalition politique annonce son boycott des prochaines législatives |url=https://news.gnet.tn/tunisie-une-nouvelle-coalition-politique-annonce-son-boycott-des-prochaines-legislatives/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Gnet news |language=fr-FR}} The Soumoud coalition democratic and progressive forces to come together to prepare common candidacies for the legislative elections, and proposing a roadmap in the event of victory,{{Cite web |date=2022-07-31 |title=Tunisie : Abir Moussi tente l'impossible, rassembler une opposition éclatée |url=https://kapitalis.com/tunisie/2022/07/31/tunisie-abir-moussi-tente-limpossible-rassembler-une-opposition-eclatee/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Kapitalis |language=fr-FR}} the [[Free Destourian Party]] (PDL) finally announced on 7 September that it would not take part in the legislative elections, considering them a "state crime", and considering the unilateral revision of the election law as an "illegal".{{Cite web |date=2022-09-07 |title=Abir Moussi : Le Parti destourien libre ne participera pas aux élections législatives (Vidéo) |url=https://www.tunisienumerique.com/abir-moussi-le-parti-destourien-libre-ne-participera-pas-aux-elections-legislatives-video/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Tunisie Numerique |language=fr-FR}} It The party also announces a nationwide day of anger and protest on 17 September.{{Cite web |date=2022-09-11 |title=PDL : 17 septembre, journée de colère dans tout le pays |url=https://www.webdo.tn/fr/actualite/national/pdl-17-septembre-journee-de-colere-dans-tout-le-pays/131216 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=www.webdo.tn |language=fr}} The boycott of the elections by |title=Afek Tounès appelle Saïed à une présidentielle anticipée |url=https://www.mosaiquefm.net/fr/actualite-politique-tunisie/1088517/afek-tounes-appelle-saied-a-une-presidentielle-anticipee |language=fr}} and the National Alliance party of [[Néji Jalloul]] are also boycotting the legislative election.{{Cite web |title=L'Alliance nationale boycotte les législatives |url=https://www.mosaiquefm.net/fr/actualite-politique-tunisie/1091724/l-alliance-nationale-boycotte-les-legislatives |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=RadioMosaiqueFM |date=3 October 2022 2022 |language=fr}} === Party participation === On 29 September 2022, ISIE spokesperson Mohamed Tlili Mansri announced that political parties are banned from campaigning for the legislative elections and that candidates must campaign individually.{{Cite web |title=Tunisie: Les partis politiques interdits de faire campagne pour les législatives anticipées |url=https://www.espacemanager.com/tunisie-les-partis-politiques-interdits-de-faire-campagne-pour-les-legislatives-anticipees.html |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Espace Manager |language=fr}} He adds that it is forbidden for candidates to indicate in their application file the party they represent.{{Cite web |last=DERMECH |first=Abdelkrim |date=2022-10-01 |title=Législatives anticipées : Quel avenir pour les partis politiques ? |url=https://lapresse.tn/140801/legislatives-anticipees-quel-avenir-pour-les-partis-politiques/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=La Presse de Tunisie |language=fr-FR}} Following the denunciation of these prohibitions by politicians,{{Cite web |date=2022-09-30 |title=Legislatives 2022: L'Alliance pour la Tunisie dénonce l'interdiction des partis de mener des campagnes électorales |work=Directinfo |url=https://directinfo.webmanagercenter.com/2022/09/30/legislatives-2022-lalliance-pour-la-tunisie-denonce-linterdiction-des-partis-de-mener-des-campagnes-electorales/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |language=fr-FR}}{{Cite web |date=2022-11-30 |title=Issam chebbi: Les restrictions excessives aux partis confirment l'illégitimité des prochaines législatives |url=https://www.tuniscope.com/article/340991/actualites/politique/issam-410217 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=tuniscope.com |language=fr-FR}} the Head of State specifies that political parties can participate in the electoral campaign but only by supporting them in a personal capacity.{{Cite web |last=DERMECH |first=Abdelkrim |date=2022-10-04 |title=Les partis politiques et les législatives du 17 décembre 2022 : Les doutes, enfin, levés |url=https://lapresse.tn/141044/les-partis-politiques-et-les-legislatives-du-17-decembre-2022-les-doutes-enfin-leves/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=La and program of the political party during their campaign.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-04 |title=ISIE-Elections législatives: Les candidats peuvent utiliser les logos des partis politiques |url=https://www.mosaiquefm.net/fr/actualite-politique-tunisie/1090521/legislatives-pas-de-campagne-pour-les-partis |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=RadioMosaiqueFM |date=29 September 2022 sponsorship case === On 6 October 2022, the ISIE announced that some potential legislative candidates had attempted to illegally obtain sponsorships by exploiting public resources, abusing their power or in return for compensation. An investigation is therefore opened and the suspected persons are arrested.{{Cite web |title=Législatives: Tentatives de parrainages illégaux et arrestations... |url=https://www.mosaiquefm.net/fr/elections-legislatives-2022-tunisie/1092696/legislatives-tentatives-de-parrainages-illegaux-et-arrestations |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=RadioMosaiqueFM |date=6 October 2022 |language=fr}}{{Cite web |last=Benyounes |first=Cherif |date=2022-10-06 |title=Législatives tunisiennes : Enquête judiciaire à l'encontre de candidats ayant tenté d'obtenir des parrainages illégalement |url=https://kapitalis.com/tunisie/2022/10/06/legislatives-tunisiennes-enquete-judiciaire-a-lencontre-de-candidats-ayant-tente-dobtenir-des-parrainages-illegalement/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Kapitalis |language=fr-FR}} According to the President of the Republic, among the offenses are the refusal of the legalization of signatures of sponsorships by municipal councils, the facilitation of the legalization of signatures for certain candidates, or the fact of "terrorizing citizens" to obtain their sponsorships. Faced with this affair, [[Kais Saied]] compares sponsorships to "merchandise that is sold and bought" and evokes, on 8 October 2022, the need to amend the electoral law a second time.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-08 |title=Tunisie : Les parrainages poussent Kais Saied à amender la loi électorale ! |url=https://www.webdo.tn/fr/actualite/national/tunisie-les-parrainages-poussent-kais-saied-a-amender-la-loi-electorale/186702 |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=www.webdo.tn |language=fr}} The president of the ISIE reacts to this statement by saying that it would be preferable not to amend the law when the electoral period has begun and sponsorships have already been collected. It specifies that it will not be possible to renounce the sponsorships that the candidates received before a potential second amendment.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-10 |title=Tunisie : "Il vaut mieux ne pas toucher à la loi électorale, en cette période" (Bouaskar) |url=https://news.gnet.tn/tunisie-il-vaut-mieux-ne-pas-toucher-a-la-loi-electorale-en-cette-periode-bouaskar/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Gnet news |language=fr-FR}} He also insists on the importance of examining the situation before making technical adjustments to the law and of consulting the ISIE at this stage of the campaign. On 10 October, the vice-president of the ISIE Maher Jedidi confirms that the presidency of the Republic is preparing a new amendment to the electoral law and that the independent body will have an advisory role when it is ready. He insists all the same on the importance of keeping the candidacy conditions as they are and that, if certain technical points were changed, the ISIE will have its say, suggesting a mistrust of such an action on the part of the president by the ISIE.{{Cite web |last=Loum |first=Souleymane |date=2022-10-10 |title=L'ISIE ose fixer une ligne rouge, vers un combat contre Saied? |url=https://www.tunisienumerique.com/lisie-ose-fixer-une-ligne-rouge-vers-un-combat-contre-saied/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=Tunisie |language=fr-FR}} ==Opinion polls== [[File:Opinion polling for the 2022 Tunisian parliamentary election.svg|thumb|800px|centre| {{columns-list|colwidth=18em| {{Legend-line|{{party color|Ennahda Movement}} solid 5px|[[Ennahda]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|Heart of Tunisia}} solid 5px|[[Heart of Tunisia]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|Free Destourian Party}} solid 5px|[[Free Destourian Party]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|Democratic Current}} solid 5px|[[Democratic Current]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|Dignity Coalition}} solid 5px|[[Dignity Coalition]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|People's Movement (Tunisia)}} solid 5px|[[People's Movement (Tunisia)|People's Movement]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|Tahya Tounes}} solid 5px|[[Tahya Tounes]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|Afek Tounes}} solid 5px|[[Afek Tounes]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|Nidaa Tounes}} solid 5px|[[Nidaa Tounes]]}} {{Legend-line|{{party color|Popular Front (Tunisia)}} solid 5px|[[Popular Front (Tunisia)|Popular Front]]}} {{Legend-line|#2B253F solid 5px|''Party of [[Kais Saied]]''}} {{Legend-line|#B0988C solid 5px|''Party of [[Safi Saïd]]''}} }}]] Parties boycotting the election are marked in italics. General elections were held in [[Tanzania]] on 28 October 2020 to elect the [[President of Tanzania|President]] and members of [[National Assembly (Tanzania)|National Assembly]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tanzania to go to polls on October 28, National Electoral|url=https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/news/National-Electoral-Commission-releases-key-dates-for-2020-polls/1840340-5596718-1yawn6/index.html|access-date=2020-07-22|website=The Citizen|language=en}}</ref> The presidential election was won by incumbent [[John Magufuli]] of the [[Chama Cha Mapinduzi]] party.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tanzania elections: President Magufuli in landslide win amid fraud claims |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-54748332 |access-date=1 November 2020 |newspaper=BBC News |date=31 October 2020}}</ref> Magufuli died the following year.

== Background ==
In April 2019, [[Livingstone Lusinde]], an [[Member of parliament|MP]] for the ruling [[Chama Cha Mapinduzi]] party, suggested that holding a presidential election in 2020 was not a good idea due to the cost, and that the money should be used for development projects.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/news/1840340-5062318-88pn8e/index.html|title=Tanzania: Mtera MP proposes presidential election to be skipped in 2020 polls|work=[[The Citizen (Tanzania)|The Citizen]]|date=8 April 2019}}</ref> The proposal was likely made in order to keep President [[John Magufuli]] in office till 2025, with Lusinde saying "no one can defeat president Magufuli" anyway.<ref>{{cite web|date=4 September 2019|title=No one can defeat Magufuli, so no need for 2020 elections: Tanzania MP|url=https://www.africanews.com/2019/04/09/no-one-can-defeat-magufuli-so-no-need-for-2020-elections-tanzania-mp/|work=Africa News}}</ref>

Opposition parties [[Chadema]], [[Alliance for Change and Transparency]], and [[NCCR-Mageuzi]] announced they had started negotiations to form an alliance ahead of the election.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ACT Wazalendo, Chadema hint at a possible coalition in October polls|url=https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/act-wazalendo-chadema-hint-at-a-possible-coalition-in-october-polls-2710488|access-date=2021-06-02|website=The Citizen|date=31 October 2020|language=en}}</ref>

The election commission announced that the campaign would run from 26 August to 27 October 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tanzania presidential election to be held on October 28|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/7/21/tanzania-presidential-election-to-be-held-on-october-28|access-date=2021-06-02|website=www.aljazeera.com|language=en}}</ref>

== Electoral system ==
The president is elected in a single round by [[first-past-the-post voting]] for a five-year term. Article 39(1) of the [[Constitution of Tanzania|1977 Constitution]] requires candidates to be Tanzanian citizens by birth, at least 40 years old, be nominated by a political party of which they are a member, be qualified to be an MP or a member of the [[Zanzibar House of Representatives]] and not have any convictions related to tax evasion.<ref>{{cite web|date=1977|title=Constitution of Tanzania|url=http://www.judiciary.go.tz/downloads/constitution.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101217023916/http://www.judiciary.go.tz/downloads/constitution.pdf|archive-date=17 December 2010|access-date=7 July 2015|publisher=Judiciary of Tanzania|at=Article 39(1)}}</ref>

== Presidential candidates ==
=== CCM ===
{{See also|2020 Chama Cha Mapinduzi presidential primaries}}
The ruling [[Chama Cha Mapinduzi|CCM]] (and its predecessor parties) has dominated the political scene since the nation attained independence in 1961. Following the restoration of multi-party politics in 1992, it has retained its popularity and the voters' confidence, winning all of the past five general elections (held in [[1995 Tanzanian general election|1995]], [[2000 Tanzanian general election|2000]], [[2005 Tanzanian general election|2005]], [[2010 Tanzanian general election|2010]], [[2015 Tanzanian general election|2015]]).<ref>{{Cite journal|last=O'Gorman|first=Melanie|date=2012-04-01|title=Why the CCM won't lose: the roots of single-party dominance in Tanzania|journal=Journal of Contemporary African Studies|volume=30|issue=2|pages=313–333|doi=10.1080/02589001.2012.669566|s2cid=17134713|issn=0258-9001}}</ref> The previous election was won by [[John Magufuli]], who ran for re-election for his second term.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2020-06-17|title=Tanzanian President Confirms He'll Seek Re-election in October|language=en|work=Bloomberg.com|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-06-17/tanzanian-president-confirms-he-ll-seek-reelection-in-october|access-date=2020-09-07}}</ref>

=== Opposition ===

==== CHADEMA ====
The main opposition party [[Chama cha Democracia na Maendeleo]] (CHADEMA) held its general council conference in Dar es Salaam on 3 August 2020. A total of seven members completed their nomination forms for the position for the Union President.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Tanzania's opposition picks Tundu Lissu to battle Magufuli in 2020 polls|url=https://www.nation.co.ke/kenya/news/africa/tanzania-s-opposition-picks-tundu-lissu-to-battle-magufuli-in-2020-polls-1912424|access-date=2020-08-04|website=Daily Nation|language=en|archive-date=5 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805042845/https://www.nation.co.ke/kenya/news/africa/tanzania-s-opposition-picks-tundu-lissu-to-battle-magufuli-in-2020-polls-1912424|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[Tundu Lissu]], MP for Singida East<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tanzania parties start nominations ahead of October General Election|url=https://www.theeastafrican.co.ke/tea/news/east-africa/tanzania-parties-start-nominations-ahead-of-october-general-election-1442746|access-date=2021-06-02|website=The East African|date=5 July 2020|language=en}}</ref>
*[[Lazaro Nyalandu]], former Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade and MP for [[Singida]] North<ref>ippmedia.com/en/news/aspirants-drawing-individual-manifestos</ref>
*Mayrose Majige, human development specialist
*[[Isaya Mwita Charles]], mayor of [[Dar es Salaam]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.habarileo.co.tz/habari/2020-06-175ee9fef06dac5.aspx|title=Chadema yataja 11 uchaguzi wa Rais}}</ref>
*Leonard Manyama, political analyst<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eatv.tv/news/current-affairs/mtia-nia-wa-urais-chademaadaihanaanayemhofia|title = Mtia nia wa Urais CHADEMA adai hana anayemhofia | East Africa Television|date = 18 June 2020}}</ref>
*Gasper Mwanalyela, advocate for the [[High Court of Tanzania]]
*Richmond Simba, advocate

A total of 453 of 456 party general council delegates attended the conference. The three names passed on by the central committee for the general council to vote on were, [[Tundu Lissu]] (405 votes), [[Lazaro Nyalandu]] (36 votes) and Mayrose Majige (1 vote),<ref name=":0" /> with Lissu chosen as CHADEMA's Union presidential candidate.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Maina|first=Mwangi|title=Tundu Lissu to fly Chadema's presidential ticket|url=https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/africa/article/2001381149/tundu-lissu-to-fly-chadema-s-presidential-ticket|access-date=2021-06-02|website=The Standard|language=en}}</ref>

==== ACT-Wazalendo ====
[[Alliance for Change and Transparency]]-Wazalendo part held their central committee elections on 5 August 2020. The party's 420 central committee members nominated ex foreign minister [[Bernard Membe]] with 97.61% vote as the union presidential candidate. Membe was expelled from CCM earlier in the year and moved over to ACT to be able to run for president.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Membe to face Magufuli in October polls as ACT presidential|url=https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/news/Membe-to-face-Magufuli-in-October-polls-as-ACT/1840340-5604784-46isgrz/index.html|access-date=2020-08-06|website=The Citizen|language=en}}</ref>

== Conduct ==
On 24 October 2020 the opposition claimed that the government was interfering in the election by making it more difficult to accredit thousands of opposition electoral observers, whose job is to ensure that the election is fair.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2020-10-29|title=Tanzania opposition loses key seats in vote marred by fraud claim|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/29/tanzania-opposition-loses-key-seats-in-vote-marred-by-fraud-claim|access-date=2020-10-30|website=Al Jazeera|language=en}}</ref> The [[National Electoral Commission (Tanzania)|National Electoral Commission]], whose members are appointed by the president, barred Lissu from campaigning after he said Magufuli had organised a meeting with election officials.<ref>{{cite web|title=Observers say Tanzania's presidential vote is already flawed|url=https://apnews.com/article/virus-outbreak-john-magufuli-tanzania-elections-nairobi-33bce46190d61be88f839f2f98e42945|first=Tom|last=Odula|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=24 October 2020|access-date=24 October 2020}}</ref> From 27 October, the Tanzania Communication Regulatory Authority (TCRA) blocked several popular social media websites to restrict communication amid violence in the islands of Zanzibar, where dozens have been shot dead and tens have been injured by the police and other security forces.<ref name=":1" />

According to Al Jazeera, "The election was marred by allegations of arrests of candidates and protesters, restrictions on agents of political parties to access polling stations, multiple voting, pre-ticking of ballots, and widespread blocking of social media." A local elections watchdog group noted a heavy deployment of military and police whose conduct created a “climate of fear”.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Magufuli wins re-election in Tanzania; opposition cries foul |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/30/magufuli-wins-re-election-in-tanzania-says-electoral-commission |access-date=2023-08-03 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref>

== International reactions ==
The Tanzania electoral watch panel,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tanzania electoral watch panel condemns arrest of opposition leaders|url=https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/tanzania-electoral-watch-panel-condemns-arrest-of-opposition-leaders-2729766|access-date=2021-06-02|website=The Citizen|date=4 November 2020|language=en}}</ref> U.S. State Department,<ref>{{Cite web|title=US State Department calls for investigation into poll irregularities|url=https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/us-state-department-calls-for-investigation-into-poll-irregularities-2729754|access-date=2021-06-02|website=The Citizen|date=4 November 2020|language=en}}</ref> Commonwealth,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Common Wealth ready to help, urges Tanzania to investigate polls irregularities|url=https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/common-wealth-ready-to-help-urges-tanzania-to-investigate-polls-irregularities--2729762|access-date=2021-06-02|website=The Citizen|date=4 November 2020|language=en}}</ref> and European Union<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tanzania – Declaration by the High Representative on behalf of the EU on the elections in Tanzania|url=https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2020/11/02/tanzania-declaration-by-the-high-representative-on-behalf-of-the-eu-on-the-elections-in-tanzania/|access-date=2020-11-13|website=www.consilium.europa.eu|language=en}}</ref> were very critical about the elections.

On 10 November 2020, [[OHCHR]] published a declaration on the electoral process and its consequences.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OHCHR {{!}} UN rights chief disturbed by harassment of opposition following Tanzania elections|url=https://www.ohchr.org/en/NewsEvents/Pages/DisplayNews.aspx?NewsID=26489&LangID=E|access-date=2020-11-13|website=www.ohchr.org}}</ref> It was at once answered by Tanzania government.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tanzania government reacts to UN concern over rights|url=https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/tanzania-government-reacts-to-un-concern-over-rights-3018302|access-date=2021-06-02|website=The Citizen|date=11 November 2020|language=en|archive-date=11 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111131628/https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/tanzania-government-reacts-to-un-concern-over-rights-3018302|url-status=live}}</ref>

banned|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://jp.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-uganda-election-idUSKBN23N24K|access-date=2020-09-18|archive-date=2020-11-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201115172733/https://jp.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-uganda-election-idUSKBN23N24K|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|last=Biryabarema|first=Elias|date=2020-07-21|title=Uganda's Museveni seeks re-election to extend rule to four decades|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-uganda-politics-idUSKCN24M0YH|access-date=2020-09-18|archive-date=2020-07-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200731001056/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-uganda-politics-idUSKCN24M0YH|url-status=live}} The Electoral Commission announced Incumbent President [[Yoweri Museveni]], the incumbent ruling since 1986, as the winner with 59% of the vote, although the [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] qualified the electoral process as "fundamentally flawed"{{Cite news|last=Milliken|first=David|last2=Fick|first2=Maggie|editor-last=Kerry|editor-first=Frances|title=Uganda's Museveni wins sixth term, rival alleges fraud|access-date=2025-12-06|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-uganda-election-idUSKBN29M04E|website=Reuters|date=2021-01-17}} and Africa Elections Watch said they observed irregularities. The official [[voter turnout]] was 57%{{cite news |title=Museveni declared winner of disputed Uganda presidential election |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/16/ugandas-museveni-declared-winner-of-presidential-election |access-date=2025-12-06|work=Al Jazeera English |date=2021-01-17|orig-date=Originally published 2021-01-16|language=en |archive-date=2021-01-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116125041/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/16/ugandas-museveni-declared-winner-of-presidential-election |url-status=live }} but was questioned as 409 polling stations were reported as having 100% voter turnout.{{Cite web|title=409 Polling Stations had 100% Voter Turnout, Giving Museveni 95.8%|url=https://ugandaradionetwork.com/story/409-polling-stations-had-100-voter-turnout-giving-museveni-95-8|website=URN|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220101131224/https://ugandaradionetwork.com/story/409-polling-stations-had-100-voter-turnout-giving-museveni-95-8|archive-date=2022-01-01|url-status=dead}}{{Cite news|title=Election observers baffled by 100% voter turnout|work=Observer|url=https://observer.ug/news/headlines/68513-election-observers-baffled-by-100-voter-turnout-at-409-polling-stations|date=2021-02-17|access-date=2025-12-06}} ==Electoral system== The [[President of Uganda]] is elected using the [[two-round system]], with candidates needing to receive at least 50% of the vote to be elected in the first round. Chapter 142 of the Presidential Elections Act of 2000 stipulates that presidential candidates must be a citizen of Uganda by birth and be qualified to be an MP.{{Cite web|title=Presidential {{as written|Ele|ctons [sic]}} Act 2000 {{!}} Uganda Legal Information Institute|url=https://ulii.org/ug/legislation/consolidated-act/142|access-date=2020-09-18|website=ulii.org|archive-date=2020-11-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201115162005if_/https://ulii.org/ug/legislation/consolidated-act/142|url-status=dead}} Candidates are also required to be of [[sound mind]] and have no formal connection with the [[Electoral Commission of Uganda]]. Term limits were abolished in 2005.{{Cite web|last=Goitom|first=Hanibal|date=2012-04-25|title=Uganda: Proposal to Re-Introduce Presidential Term Limits {{!}} Global Legal Monitor|url=https://www.loc.gov/law/foreign-news/article/uganda-proposal-to-re-introduce-presidential-term-limits/|access-date=2020-09-18|website=www.loc.gov|archive-date=2019-09-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190907150357/http://www.loc.gov/law/foreign-news/article/uganda-proposal-to-re-introduce-presidential-term-limits/|url-status=live}} The elections are supervised by the Electoral Commission of Uganda.{{Cite web|title=IFES Election Guide {{!}} Elections: Uganda President 2016|url=https://www.electionguide.org/elections/id/2754/|access-date=2020-09-18|website=www.electionguide.org|archive-date=2020-09-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919225026/https://www.electionguide.org/elections/id/2754/|url-status=live}} The [[Parliament of Uganda]] has a total of 529 seats, including 353 representatives elected using [[first-past-the-post voting]] in [[List of constituencies in Uganda|single winner constituencies]]. Using the same method, 146 seats reserved for women are filled, with one seat per [[Districts of Uganda|district]]. Finally, 30 seats are indirectly filled via special electoral colleges: 10 by the army, 5 by youths, 5 by elders, 5 by unions, and 5 by people with disabilities. In each of these groups, at least one woman must be elected (at least two for the army group).{{Cite web|url=https://www.ilo.org/dyn/natlex/docs/ELECTRONIC/44038/90491/F206329993/UGA44038.pdf|title=Constitution|access-date=2021-01-13|archive-date=2020-09-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918153033/https://www.ilo.org/dyn/natlex/docs/ELECTRONIC/44038/90491/F206329993/UGA44038.pdf|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.ec.or.ug/sites/default/files/press/VET%20Handbook%202020.pdf|title=Electoral handbook|access-date=2021-01-13|archive-date=2020-11-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129045142/https://www.ec.or.ug/sites/default/files/press/VET%20Handbook%202020.pdf|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.electionguide.org/elections/id/3613/#_ftn1|title=IFES Election Guide | Elections: Uganda National Assembly 2021|website=www.electionguide.org|access-date=2021-01-14|archive-date=2021-01-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122193008/https://www.electionguide.org/elections/id/3613/#_ftn1|url-status=live}} ==Presidential candidates== Eleven candidates were registered to contest the election.[https://www.ec.or.ug/sites/default/files/campaign/Presidential%20Campaign%20Programme%20%28Revised%20on%2026.12.2020%29%20%281%29.pdf Presidential elections 2020/2021]{{Dead link|date=March 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Electoral Commission # [[Yoweri Museveni]], [[National Resistance Movement]] # [[Bobi Wine]], [[National Unity Platform]] # John Katumba, Independent # [[Willy Mayambala]], Independent # [[Fred Mwesigye]], Independent # [[Henry Tumukunde]], Independent # [[Joseph Kabuleta]], Independent # [[Nancy Kalembe]], Independent # [[Patrick Oboi Amuriat]], [[Forum for Democratic Change]] # [[Mugisha Muntu]], [[Alliance for National Transformation]] # [[Norbert Mao]], [[Democratic Party (Uganda)|Democratic Party]] ==Campaign== Campaigning was stopped in [[Mbarara]], [[Kabarole]], [[Luweero]], [[Kasese]], [[Masaka]], [[Wakiso]], [[Jinja, Uganda|Jinja]], [[Kalungu, Uganda|Kalungu]], [[Kazo, Uganda|Kazo]], [[Kampala|Kampala City]] and [[Tororo]] on 26 December 2020. The government said it was to prevent spread of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda|COVID-19 pandemic]], but critics said it was because of the popularity of the opposition in those areas. Crowds had previously been limited to 200 people.{{cite news |title=Uganda halts campaigning for January 14 vote in several districts |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/12/26/uganda-suspends-campaigning-in-several-districts-ahead-of-polls |access-date=December 26, 2020 |work=aljazeera.com |publisher=Al Jazeera English |date=December 26, 2020 |language=en |archive-date=December 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201226192549/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/12/26/uganda-suspends-campaigning-in-several-districts-ahead-of-polls |url-status=live }} When asked what he wanted to accomplish that he hadn't already done after 35 years in power, Museveni said he wanted to work for the economic integration in Africa, and to change the Ugandan culture of not working hard. He said in other countries, a harsh environment of competition pushed people to work, "but here, fools can survive".{{cite web |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/01/12/955938674/ugandas-museveni-faces-tough-challenge-in-presidential-election |title=Uganda's Museveni Faces Tough Challenge In Presidential Election |date=12 Jan 2021 |author=Eyder Peralta |access-date=30 January 2021 |archive-date=27 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127135129/https://www.npr.org/2021/01/12/955938674/ugandas-museveni-faces-tough-challenge-in-presidential-election |url-status=live }} ==Conduct== ===International observers=== The [[European Union]] did not deploy observers (EOM—election observer mission) because previous recommendations from their 2016 mission had been ignored.{{cite news |last1=Biryabarema |first1=Elias |title=EU says won't monitor Uganda election, limiting poll's international scrutiny |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/eu-says-wont-monitor-uganda-123043127.html |access-date=November 16, 2020 |work=Yahoo! News |agency=Reuters |date=November 16, 2020 |archive-date=November 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116155004/https://www.yahoo.com/news/eu-says-wont-monitor-uganda-123043127.html |url-status=live }} On 13 January 2021, the United States cancelled its observation of Uganda's presidential election, saying the voting will lack transparency and accountability.{{cite news |title=U.S. cancels its observation of Uganda's presidential election |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/us-cancels-its-observation-of-ugandas-presidential-election/ar-BB1cIum9?ocid=ob-fb-enus-1541512262291 |access-date=January 13, 2021 |work=msn.com |agency=Reuters |date=January 13, 2021 |archive-date=January 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116200055/https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/us-cancels-its-observation-of-ugandas-presidential-election/ar-BB1cIum9?ocid=ob-fb-enus-1541512262291 |url-status=live }} ===Arrests of Bobi Wine=== On 18 November 2020, opposition candidate Bobi Wine was arrested for allegedly violating COVID-19 protocols during his presidential campaign in Uganda. The National Unity Platform claimed that the continued arrests of its members were intended to stifle their ability to campaign rather than to follow COVID protocols. Supporters of Wine took to the streets of [[Kampala]], clashing with security forces. This led to violent protests in which 100 people died and more than 500 were injured.{{Cite news|last1=Athumani|first1=Halima|last2=Wroughton|first2=Lesley|title=37 dead in Uganda protests after arrest of presidential candidate Bobi Wine|language=en-US|work=[[The Washington Post]]|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/uganda-protests-bobi-wine/2020/11/20/efe106ec-2aa6-11eb-9c21-3cc501d0981f_story.html|access-date=2021-01-10|issn=0190-8286|archive-date=2021-01-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113010908/https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/uganda-protests-bobi-wine/2020/11/20/efe106ec-2aa6-11eb-9c21-3cc501d0981f_story.html|url-status=live|date=2020-11-20}}{{Cite web|last=Ntale|first=Samson|title=Protests after the arrest of Bobi Wine, Ugandan presidential candidate|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/18/africa/bobi-wine-arrest-nov-18-intl/index.html|access-date=2021-01-10|website=CNN|date=2020-11-18}} Wine was arrested again on 30 December on [[Kalangala|Kalangala Island]], where a rally he was holding was cut short by police. Police broke up the rally using tear gas and Wine was put under house arrest at his home in Kampala.{{Cite web|title=Uganda police arrest Bobi Wine, tear gas supporters|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/12/30/uganda-police-arrest-bobi-wine-tear-gas-supporters|access-date=2021-01-10|website=Al Jazeera|language=en|archive-date=2021-01-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112033645/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/12/30/uganda-police-arrest-bobi-wine-tear-gas-supporters|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|last=Akinwotu|first=Emmanuel|date=2021-01-07|title=Bobi Wine confronted by Ugandan police during appeal for ICC inquiry|language=en-GB|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jan/07/bobi-wine-confronted-by-ugandan-police-during-appeal-for-icc-inquiry|access-date=2021-01-10|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=2021-01-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109085243/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jan/07/bobi-wine-confronted-by-ugandan-police-during-appeal-for-icc-inquiry|url-status=live}} During his campaign, several aides, bodyguards and members of his entourage were arrested, jailed and killed.{{Cite web|title=Uganda's Bobi Wine says his bodyguard was 'deliberately' run over and killed|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/27/africa/uganda-bobi-wine-bodyguard-intl-hnk/index.html|access-date=2021-01-10|website=CNN|archive-date=2021-01-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131145552/https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/27/africa/uganda-bobi-wine-bodyguard-intl-hnk/index.html|url-status=live}} ===Social media and internet block=== On 13 January 2021, a day before the elections and a day after Facebook closed "fake" accounts it said were linked to the government, the communications regulator in Uganda ordered all telecoms firms to block access to social media and messaging apps in retaliation.{{Cite news|date=2021-01-12|title=Uganda elections 2021: Social media blocked ahead of poll|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-55640405|access-date=2021-01-13}} The Ugandan government denied the charges and accused Facebook of meddling in the election saying "I think they are playing the usual games, we know that they have a side in this election perhaps."{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-55623722|title=Uganda elections 2021: Facebook shuts government-linked accounts|work=BBC News|date=January 11, 2021|access-date=January 13, 2021|archive-date=January 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113021008/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-55623722|url-status=live}} At 5 pm on 13 January, the government ordered a complete internet shut-down, which came into effect at 7 pm. [[Amnesty International]]'s deputy regional director condemned the move, saying that it was "clearly intended to silence the few accredited election observers, opposition politicians, human rights defenders, activists, journalists, and bloggers who are monitoring the elections".{{cite news |date=14 January 2021 |url=https://qz.com/africa/1957137/uganda-cuts-off-internet-ahead-of-election-polls-opening/ |work=Quartz Africa |first=Stephen |last=Kafeero |title=Uganda has cut off its entire internet hours to its election polls opening |access-date=16 January 2021 |archive-date=15 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115001828/https://qz.com/africa/1957137/uganda-cuts-off-internet-ahead-of-election-polls-opening/ |url-status=live }} ===Allegations of fraud=== On 15 January (the day after the election), Bobi Wine announced that Ugandan security forces had surrounded and breached his compound after he had alleged that the elections had been "marred by fraud and violence".{{Cite news|last=Dahir|first=Abdi Latif|date=2021-01-15|title=Ugandan Forces Surround Home of Leading Opposition Figure|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/15/world/africa/uganda-election-bobi-wine.html|access-date=2021-01-16|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=2021-01-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115224724/http://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/15/world/africa/uganda-election-bobi-wine.html|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|last=Athumani|first=Halima|date=15 January 2021|title=Uganda Soldiers Enter Home of Opposition Leader After He Alleges Election Fraud|url=https://www.voanews.com/a/africa_uganda-soldiers-enter-home-opposition-leader-after-he-alleges-election-fraud/6200769.html|access-date=2021-01-16|website=Voice of America|language=en}} Wine said he had video proof of voting fraud and would share the videos as soon as internet connections were restored. He accused Museveni of fabricating the results and called the poll "the most fraudulent election in the history of Uganda... The entire process has been conducted in [the] dark and it lacks transparency," Katana, head agent of Bobi Wine's National Unity Platform, said "From the beginning, we were assured by the electoral commission that each candidate or their agents will receive copies of the results from the districts before they are transmitted to the national tally centre, so we are able to verify when they are reading here – and that was not done." On February 1, the legal team for opposition leader Bobi Wine filed a Supreme Court lawsuit, asking it to declare President Yoweri Museveni's re-election rigged. George Musisi, a member of Wine's legal team, said that the National United Platform (NUP) had amassed "glaring evidence" proving that the election result was invalid. "There was outright ballot-stuffing, there was intimidation of NUP agents and supporters, some were arrested on the eve of [last month's] election, there was pre-ticking of ballots," said Musisi.{{Cite web|url=https://www.dw.com/en/uganda-election-bobi-wine-challenges-result-in-court/a-56405583|title = Uganda election: Bobi Wine challenges result in court | DW | 01.02.2021}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20210201-uganda-s-opposition-leader-bobi-wine-files-election-challenge-in-court|title=Uganda's opposition leader Bobi Wine files election challenge in court|website=France 24|date=2021-02-01|access-date=2025-12-06}} ==Results== ===President=== Justice Simon Mugenyi Byabakama, chair of the Electoral Commission, declared Museveni the winner of the presidential election on 16 January, stating that he won almost 59% of the vote, with Wine taking 35%. Voter turnout was 57%. Byabakama said that it had been a peaceful election.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-55689665 |website=[[BBC News]] |title=Uganda: Veteran leader Yoweri Museveni declared election winner |date=16 January 2021 |access-date=16 January 2021 |archive-date=21 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121231701/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-55689665 |url-status=live }} Speaking before the results were announced, Wine told reporters that it was "the most fraudulent election in the history of Uganda" and also accused Museveni of putting him "under siege", as security forces surrounded his home. Museveni denied these claims in a televised address after being proclaimed the winner, saying that the votes had been machine-counted and that it "may turn out to be the most cheating-free election since 1962".{{cite news |work=[[The Guardian]] |title=Museveni declared election winner in Uganda as rival Bobi Wine alleges fraud |first1=Emmanuel |last1=Akinwotu |first2=Samuel |last2=Okiror
